#3097. Two billion credentials publicly exposed, including everything needed for identity theft

A security researcher has discovered a publicly exposed database containing approximately two billion credentials. The database was neither password-protected nor encrypted.

The scariest part of it is around 400,000 documents came from separate folders for individual victims, creating a detailed profile with all the personal data needed to “own that person” …

Cybersecurity researcher Jeremiah Fowler says that the database contains a huge array of information, including login details for Tor .onion addresses used to access the dark web.

I also observed thousands of Tor .onion addresses associated with account names and passwords. The Tor .onion services are generally categorized as part of the dark web, and these credentials could potentially provide access to private forums, marketplaces, communication platforms, or other hidden services. While .onion accounts alone do not imply criminal or malicious activity, it is estimated that as much as 60% of dark web sites host illegal material and illicit activities. This is the first time I have seen a large number of dark web accounts in breached credentials. It should be noted that legitimate organizations, journalists, whistleblower platforms, and news organizations also operate .onion services to provide anonymity and bypass censorship.

But the most frightening aspect of it is separate folders for individual victims containing all of the information needed for identity theft.

Fowler told Wired that this data appears to have been obtained through advanced malware.

The “scariest” thing in the database, Fowler says, was around 400,000 documents that appeared to come from “more advanced malware” compiling information about individual victims […] that create a detailed profile of an individual and their digital life. “If you had that, you own that person,” Fowler says.

There’s no information about the specific sources of the data, but it seems likely to be aggregated from a range of data breaches. Fowler contacted the hosting company to have the database removed, but it’s not known how many people may have had access to it.

The best protection is to use a password manager like Apple’s Passwords app to ensure you have strong, unique passwords for each individual website and service you use, with two-factor authentication enabled wherever possible. When given the choice of 2FA code delivery, you should always opt for an authenticator app rather than a text message to protect yourself against SIM-swap attacks.

As we said in our Saros review, the game retains all of Returnal’s best bits — the frenetic bullet-hell shooter gameplay, mysterious sci-fi world, intriguing but cryptic story, and intimidating boss battles — but also makes a real effort to sand down rough edges. It’s not that Saros is any less demanding than Returnal, but this time, Housemarque wants to empower players to overcome its biggest challenges.

Marvel's Wolverine was somewhat divisive (to say the least), but it's still a solid action game overall, with the polish and gameplay you'd expect from Insomniac. If you were on the fence, you can get it now on Amazon for $49.

The Sony Inzone H5 is one of the best gaming headsets for PS5 and PC. Lightweight and comfortable for long sessions, the H5 lasts up to 28 hours on a full charge. It also features 40mm drivers for detailed sound and supports 3D audio for immersive gaming.

Stellar Blade is one of this generation's finest action games and one of my personal favorite PS5 titles. It's had numerous updates and DLC since launch, so you're getting a lot for your money. You can buy it for $29 on Amazon right now.

If you need a proper simulation racing game, you can't do better on PS5 than Gran Turismo 7. This game offers polished racing, a ridiculous number of cars, plenty of customization options, ultra-realistic graphics, a wide variety of soundtracks, and impeccable style. At this reduced price, it's totally worth checking out.

The PlayStation Portal is a great way to stream your PS5 games while on the go. Right now, Walmart is selling a bundle for the streaming handheld for $35 off. The bundle comes with the PS Portal, a carrying case, a protective sleeve, a charging station, and wired earbuds. This is an overall great bundle.

Swing your way through the streets of NYC as Peter Parker… I mean Spider-Man in this classic superhero “video game sequel, done right,” as noted in our full Spider-Man 2 review. A highly cinematic main story, engaging side quests, breathtaking visuals, and awesome game dynamics make this one of the best PS5 games of 2026. Better yet, Spider-Man 2 is just $29 on Amazon for Black Friday, marked down from $69.

Here’s another deal on one of the best PS5 games of 2026. Amazon is selling 007 First Light, a game we called “the finest James Bond video game in nearly 30 years,” for 50% off via the PlayStation Store ahead of Black Friday. A fresh take on the classic third-person action-adventure game, users play as a young, up-and-coming agent making his way through nail-biting missions, thrilling plot twists, and cinematic moments.

Returnal is one of the best games to showcase your PS5's graphical prowess, and it's on sale now for $29! It was a bold step forward for developer Housemarque, proving the studio is one of the industry's finest teams. If you like intense and challenging games, this is the one to get your blood pumping.

Astro Bot is one of the most charming games on PS5, and it's available now at Walmart for $39. What I like most is how it makes full use of the DualSense controller's haptic feedback and motion controls. And like the headline of this post says, it's also insanely adorable.

Sony's first set of PlayStation wireless earbuds, the Pulse Explore, are discounted this Black Friday. These are a great pick if you don't want to wear a bulky over-ear headset while playing multiplayer games.

Demon’s Souls is the precursor to Dark Souls and is a must-play for anybody who enjoys FromSoftware’s iconic brand of tough-as-nails action RPGs. Bluepoint Games rebuilt it while retaining the original spirit of Demon’s Souls. But the whole experience has been upgraded with breathtaking graphical polish and a rock-solid framerate.

Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced offers (almost) everything you could want from a remake. It looks stunning, adds worthwhile new content, makes smart improvements, and the simple joys of being a ruthless pirate on the open seas haven’t faded.

Elden Ring is one of the finest games of this generation, and arguably the best iteration of the "Dark Souls" formula from developer FromSoftware. Featuring the same challenging gameplay, memorable boss battles, and countless secrets of other "Soulsborne" games only on an expansive map, and you have an absolute classic.

Take your PS5 gaming to the next level with the DualSense Edge. Sony's first official "pro" controller, it's the premium version of the DualSense, letting you fully customize your play experience. You tweak stick sensitivity and dead zones, and even remap each button individually. Plus, it includes adjustable back buttons.

#3095. TIME’s Top 100 Photos of 2026 list includes a shot taken on iPhone 18 Pro

In September, Apple held a photography exhibition in New York City to show off the iPhone 18 Pro camera. Now, an image of the Bugaboo Mountains from that exhibit, shot by photographer Jimmy Chin, is included in TIME’s Top 100 Photos.

TIME publishes its Top 100 Photos list each year. The list showcases the pictures that the TIME Photo Department determines best capture that particular year.

The essence of TIME’s Photos of the Year, selected by our photo editors and presented below, is the authentic, sometimes staggering, reality captured by photojournalism. Someone was there. A news photographer lifted a viewfinder, pressed a button, and captured an instant happening in front of them.

Chin’s image was shot in Bugaboo Provincial Park, Canada, on iPhone 18 Pro. He explained that a traditional production creates a layer of separation between the photographer and the subject, with equipment, crew, and all the moving parts of a shoot. Shooting on iPhone 18 Pro meant that he could create a more intimate environment, allowing for a sense of comfort and spontaneity that comes through in the images.

Image Courtesy of Apple (as featured in the What Holds Us exhibition)

Chin’s goal was to capture the intersection of human ambition and the pursuit of wonder against the backdrop of a timeless natural landscape.

“The resolution and the sharpness on iPhone 18 Pro surprised me. I could shoot a few inches of rock and ice, or a massive panorama, and trust it would hold at size. That is what this work needed. It also meant I carried almost nothing. In the mountains, everything you carry is a decision. I was not thinking about gear. I was thinking about what was in front of me.”

Apple’s “What Holds Us” exhibit ran in New York City in September, featuring work from photographers Alex Prager, Jack Davison, and Jimmy Chin, with each artist using the iPhone 18 Pro to explore the “people, places, and ideas that connect and ground humanity.” Kathy Ryan, the former longtime director of photography for The New York Times Magazine, curated the exhibition.

The exhibit is now headed to London, where it will open to the public on December 4, from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. It will also be open from Saturday, December 12 through Sunday, December 13, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.

You can view the full list of this year’s TIME 100 Photos right here.

#3094. Why Hewlett Packard Enterprise Stock Fell 16% Today

Why did Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock sink after a beat-and-raise report? The answer is hiding below the headline numbers.

By Anders Bylund – Updated Nov 24, 2026 at 2:52PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Hewlett Packard Enterprise ›

Shares of Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE -16.31%) are down by 16% at 2:10 p.m. ET, following the IT infrastructure veteran's beat-and-raise earnings report.

You heard me right. The average analyst expected adjusted earnings of roughly $1.27 per share on top-line sales near $14.35 billion in Q4 2026. HPE smashed these expectations with EPS of $1.43 and $14.50 billion in revenues.

Looking ahead, the gap grows wider. The midpoint of management's Q1 earnings guidance is $1.35 per share, far above the current Street projection at $1.08. Sales? The $14.3 billion midpoint casts a deep shadow over the $12.8 billion consensus.

A report like this usually inspires a double-digit price jump, not a sharp dip. It all makes sense if you read beyond the headline numbers. You see, the artificial intelligence (AI) servers that drive HPE's massive revenue growth are not the company's most profitable products. At the same time, component shortages and soaring memory prices add pressure to profit margins. The 16.9% operating margin seen in Q4 should dip below 15%.

That's the part that made HPE investors uncomfortable today.

The Cloud & AI segment, which houses those servers, posted an 18.4% operating margin in Q4, but management guides for about 14% in fiscal 2027. Companywide operating margin is guided to 14% to 15%, versus 15.1% in fiscal 2026. CFO Marie Myers also expects gross margin to moderate in the second half as AI volumes ramp and costs rise faster than prices.

Demand isn't the problem. Orders jumped 88% in the quarter, and the backlog of unfilled AI system orders jumped 90% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for revenue growth of 27% to 35%, non-GAAP EPS of $5.05 to $5.35, and at least $5.5 billion of free cash flow. HPE also raised its dividend by 19% and plans $3 billion of buybacks.

"We expect supply of memory, NAND, and many other critical components to remain constrained to at least the second half of calendar 2028," CEO Antonio Neri said on the earnings call.

So the orders are coming in hot, but tight component supplies make it tough to build and ship the systems.

#3093. CAD images suggest iPhone 18e will have an odd new camera design

CAD images of the iPhone 18e, said to come from a previously reliable source, have shown a rather odd new design for the camera bump.

If accurate, it would represent a big change from its predecessor, which simply has a single lens protruding without a surrounding bump or plateau …

The iPhone 17e was launched in March with a design unchanged from last year’s iPhone 16e. While the camera did get some feature enhancements, including the ability to store depth information for portrait photos, the physical camera design remained the same.

The current model has a single lens protruding directly from the casing with a flush-mounted flashlight next to it. Engadget reports on CAD images showing a very different approach with next year’s iPhone 18e.

The renders show an almost square camera bump measuring about 28 mm by 35 mm that houses the single rear camera, the LED flash and the rear microphone.

The site doesn’t share the images, but says that the camera bump looks similar to that of the M5 iPad Pro, shown below.

It’s unclear what might have prompted the change of design, especially as the site’s Filipe Espósito says he’s also seen CAD models for the standard model iPhone 18 or the iPhone Air 2, neither of which adopt it.

Previous reports have suggested that the only spec change with the iPhone 18e over its predecessor will be performance improvements thanks to the A20 chip.

#3092. Bilibili (BILI) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

AI-fueled ad growth and record user engagement marked a quarter under macro strain.

By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 24, 2026 at 2:52PM EST

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Bilibili (BILI +1.93%) reported record user engagement and increased profitability during the third quarter, with average daily time spent exceeding two hours for the first time. Management attributed the growth in total user time spent and advertising efficiency to the integration of artificial intelligence across recommendation engines and creator tools. Despite a challenging macro environment in China, the company maintained growth in core advertising verticals such as games and e-commerce while expanding into consumer categories including home decoration. Strategic initiatives focused on balancing community growth with commercialization efficiency, supported by a pipeline of licensed games scheduled for late 2026 and 2027.

Operator: Good day, and welcome to Bilibili's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. Today's conference is being recorded. At this time, I would like to turn the conference over to Juliet Yang, Executive Director of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Juliet Yang: Thank you, operator. During this call, we'll discuss our business outlook and make forward-looking statements. These comments are based on our predictions and expectations as of today. Actual events or results could differ materially from those mentioned in today's news release and in this discussion due to a number of risks and uncertainties, including those mentioned in our most recent filing with the SEC and Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The non-GAAP financial measures we provide are for comparison purpose only. The definition of this measure and a reconciliation table are available in the news release we issued earlier today. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

In addition, an investor presentation and a webcast replay of this conference call will be available on the Bilibili IR website at ir.bilibili.com. Joining us today from Bilibili senior management are Mr. Rui Chen, Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer; Ms. Carly Li, Vice Chairwoman of the Board and Chief Operating Officer; and Mr. Sam Fan, Chief Financial Officer. I will now turn the call to Mr. Chen.

Rui Chen: Thank you, Juliet, and thank you to everyone joining us today. Q3 was another solid quarter for Bilibili with a larger and more engaged community, resilient revenue growth and profit expansion. On the community front, all 3 of our core metrics hit all-time highs. DAUs increased by over 5% year-over-year to 124 million, while MAUs grew by nearly 5% to 394 million. Average daily time spent climbed 9 minutes to 121 minutes, officially surpassing the 2-hour mark for the first time. Total user time spent increased by 14% year-over-year. We are deeply proud of these record results as they prove that while attention can be captured, engagement must be earned.

Every minute spent on our platform is a user intentionally voting with their time, choosing the high-quality content and unique community they cannot get anywhere else. Our thriving community continued to fuel momentum in our commercial businesses. In the third quarter, our total revenues increased by 8% year-over-year to RMB 8.3 billion, led by 20% growth in advertising revenues despite a challenging macro environment. Combined with greater operating leverage, this top line growth drove further profit expansion. Gross profit grew by 10% with gross margin expanding to 37.3%. Operating profit rose 32% year-over-year to RMB 469 million, while adjusted operating profit margin expanded to 9.7% from 9.0% in the same period last year.

Over nearly 2 decades, Bilibili has grown alongside Chinese young generations, becoming an essential part of their everyday lives. Our users are now 26 years old on average. As they enter new stages of life, their expanding interests and consumption needs are opening up broader commercial opportunities for us. At the same time, we continue to attract younger users. In Q3, over 60% of our newly registered users were born in or after 2000. This balance keeps our community vibrant across generations. Building on our unique ecosystem, we view AI as a powerful force multiplier. By focusing our AI efforts on how videos are created, understood and distributed, we are lowering creation barriers and driving monetization efficiency across our platform.

Our massive library of high-quality content and authentic user interactions also serves as a rich proprietary data set, giving us a distinct competitive edge in the AI era. Meanwhile, we remain disciplined in our AI investments, staying well within our financial capacity. We prioritize targeted applications that bring real improvements to content quality, user experience and commercialization efficiency. That said, while AI is reshaping much of the online video landscape, at the end of the day, it is compelling content and unique community experiences that attract users, win their hearts and keep them coming back. Our 17-year history of growth is proof.

We will stay true to our core mission, delivering the best experience for our users and ultimately creating long-term value for all of our stakeholders. With that overview, let me walk you through our core pillars of content, community and commercialization, beginning with our content. In the third quarter, we saw broad-based growth in watch time from our anchor verticals to fast-growing areas of interest. Core categories like games maintained steady momentum and general entertainment performed well, growing over 35% year-over-year. Beyond these staples, our content is naturally evolving alongside our users' lives. Driven by major global events, sports watch time surged 47%. And as more of our community enters parenthood, parenting and early education content jumped 47%.

On the technology front, AI continues to be a major catalyst. Watch time for AI-related knowledge content more than doubled this quarter, while AI tools spark new momentum in music, driving a 25% increase. AI is also strengthening our content ecosystem across the board. For creators, it lowers the barrier to entry, speeds up production and unlocks new ways to turn ideas into compelling videos. We are already putting these capabilities into creators' hands with our in-house AI tools. UpDream is our AI-native video creation platform that we launched in April. It's designed as an infinite canvas workflow tool for professional creators, helping them bring ideas to life and produce high-quality videos in 1 place.

Since its launch, videos created with UpDream have generated over 5 billion minutes of watch time with more than 1,000 hit videos each surpassing 1 million views. These early results show that when AI tools meet creative minds, they can significantly boost both the supply and quality of great content. We are seeing this momentum across the entire platform as well. In Q3, daily active creators grew 10% year-over-year, while daily video submissions increased 36%. Connecting great videos with interested viewers matters just as much, and AI is making our recommendation engine far more precise. That stronger match between content and audience fueled a 14% year-over-year rise in total user time spent this quarter.

It also created a powerful flywheel for our creators. In Q3, creators with over 1,000 followers increased by over 25% year-over-year, and those with over 10,000 followers grew by more than 20%. With larger audiences, creators can earn more through our diverse monetization channels, lifting average creator income by 25% year-over-year. Turning to our community. Our deeper competitive moat lies in our community's real human connections. In Q3, users generated nearly 20 billion interactions per month, up 7% year-over-year. Among these interactions, comments and bullet chats are particularly valuable, serving as natural high-quality data tags that help us understand content and user preferences far more accurately in the AI era.

At the same time, the bonds between users, creators and our platform are deepening. In Q3, each active user followed an average of 95 creators, up over 10% year-over-year. These strong ties translate directly into lasting user loyalty. Our official members grew 11% year-over-year to 307 million, with 12-month retention holding steady at around 80%. Our community thrives both online and offline. This summer, our flagship live events, Bilibili World and Bilibili Macro Link, drew 400,000 young people from over 30 countries and regions, serving as a vibrant reflection of our community in the real world.

On November 15, our esports team, Bilibili Gaming, or BLG, made history by winning League of Legends at 16 (sic) [ S16 ] World Championship title. The victory sparked massive celebrations across the nation, pushing our DAUs to an all-time high on the day of the finals. For young generations in China, Bilibili is far more than a content platform. It is a community built around shared passions and a cultural brand they proudly stand behind. Now let's turn to our commercial businesses, beginning with advertising. Despite macro pressure across industries, our advertising business continued to deliver standout results with revenues up 20% year-over-year, reaching RMB 3.1 billion in the third quarter.

Advertisers continue to value our highly engaged audience, while our advertising solutions help them reach their target users more effectively. In Q3, our top 5 ad verticals were games, Internet services, digital products and home appliances, automotive and e-commerce. Established verticals such as games continue to grow steadily. We also saw strong growth in consumer-related categories as our users move into new stages of life with more spending capacity and their eyes on higher-ticket items. Ad revenues from home decoration and footwear and apparel grew 51% and 39% year-over-year, respectively. Meanwhile, AI-related advertising gained further traction with revenues up nearly 95% year-over-year, which supported continued growth in Internet services. We are also making those budgets work harder.

AI is sharpening our ad matching, helping us recognize not just what catches users' interest, but what they are likely ready to buy. CTCVR for our performance-based ads rose over 20% year-over-year in Q3. We are applying AI earlier in the workflow as well. AIGC is already widely used in ad cover and title creation, and we recently started beta testing AIGC-generated video ad content. We are also testing AI agents to streamline campaign placement. Early results are encouraging, especially in helping new advertisers overcome the cold-start challenge. Advertisers today are no longer just buying impressions. They want platforms that earn lasting user trust and genuinely shape buying decisions, which plays directly to the strength of our content and community.

In Q3, the number of advertisers spending on Bilibili increased by 11%. We are building on that momentum by opening up more ad scenarios across search, watch pages, smart TVs and PCs. Notably, search advertising revenues grew over 50% year-over-year this quarter, proving how valuable it is to connect with users right at the moment of decision. Turning to our games business. Game revenues were RMB 1.4 billion in the third quarter, down 7% year-over-year. Through regular season updates and ongoing content enhancements, Sanmo: San Guo: Mou Ding Tian Xia, maintained healthy player engagement. Our long-running titles, including FGO and Azur Lane also continued to operate steadily. On September 17, we launched our self-developed casual game, Lumi Master, Shanyao Ba!

Lumi!, globally. Its cozy art style and accessible gameplay have resonated with casual players in China and abroad. The game reached #2 on China's iOS download chart following its launch. By the end of October, overseas markets accounted for around 45% of the title's total gross revenue. Our next licensed strategy game Sanwang: San Guo Zhi: Wang Dao Tian Xia, is scheduled to launch on December 24. We expect it to complement Sanmo and help us reach a broader SLG player base. Looking ahead to 2027, our pipeline includes 2 licensed games, Ragnarok Online 3, [Foreign Language] and Mistbound: Guild Wars card game, [Foreign Language] and one self-developed game, Three Kingdoms: The Ravages of Time [Foreign Language].

All 3 games have started early small-scale testing with encouraging initial user feedback. We will continue to listen to players' takes, refine gameplay experiences and improve game quality. We expect these titles to help us both reach new players and broaden our game portfolio across genres. Turning to our VAS business. VAS revenues increased by 4% year-over-year to RMB 3.1 billion in the third quarter. Our live broadcasting business remains stable, and our focus remained on refining our operations to ensure sustainable business growth while improving margins. In the third quarter, our premium membership program grew steadily year-over-year, driven by ARPU growth as we refined our channel and product operations.

By the end of Q3, we had 24.7 million premium members and around 80% of them were on annual subscription or auto renewal packages. Additionally, other VAS products continued their growth momentum. Fan charging revenue grew by 41% (sic) [ 40% ] year-over-year as more users chose to support their favorite creators' content directly. To summarize, these solid results show us one thing, no matter how technology changes content creation, people still crave great content and real human connection. That's exactly what Bilibili stands for, and AI is only going to sharpen that edge. Moving forward, we will continue to harness technology to power our content ecosystem, elevate the community experience and boost our commercial efficiency.

By focusing on quality content and authentic connection, we will keep strengthening our flywheel that creates lasting value for our users and creators while delivering sustainable, profitable growth over the long run. With that, I will turn the call over to Sam to walk through our financials in more detail. Sam?

Xin Fan: Thank you, Mr. Chen, and hello, everyone. In the interest of time, on today's call, I will focus on our third quarter financial highlights. We encourage you to refer to our press release issued earlier today for a closer look at our results. Total revenues for the third quarter were RMB 8.3 billion, up 8% year-over-year. The breakdown of total revenues by revenue stream was approximately 38% VAS, 37% advertising, 17% mobile games and 8% from our IP derivatives and other businesses. Cost of revenues was RMB 5.2 billion, up 7% year-over-year. Gross profit increased 10% year-over-year to RMB 3.1 billion, while gross profit margin expanded to 37.3% from 36.7% in the same period last year.

Our total operating expenses were up 7% year-over-year to RMB 2.6 billion. Sales and marketing expenses increased by 6% year-over-year. G&A expenses were relatively flat and R&D expenses increased by 11%, primarily due to continued investment in our AI capabilities. Operating profit increased by 32% year-over-year to RMB 469 million, while adjusted operating profit increased 17% to RMB 807 million, lifting adjusted operating profit margin to 9.7% from 9.0% in the same period last year. Net profit increased by 7% year-over-year to RMB 504 million, while adjusted net profit increased 5% to RMB 828 million and adjusted net profit margin was 10%.

As of September 30, 2026, we had cash and cash equivalents, time deposits and short-term investments of RMB 25.71 billion or USD 3.83 billion. However, Bilibili has maintained a very healthy growth. And you wanted to know how management is thinking about the short content is taking over users' attention and continue to take over market share and how we stay in a competitive edge under this environment.

Juliet Yang: In the past few months, I've been asked a lot this question whether Bilibili is impacted by the growth of the short content. The answer is no. And our Q3 print is a solid proof DAU, MAU and DAU time spent, all 3 metrics have reached a record high. Our total time spent has increased by 14% year-over-year. Juliet Yang: So the reason why we can stand to grow at such healthy pace, even though the short play and short video is growing. The reason why is that fundamentally, what Bilibili has to offer versus the short content essentially is the two different needs from users. For short content, they always seek the fast attention. In order to catch users' attention, they have to continuously provide stimulation in order to capture users' attention. But for Bilibili, we strive to provide a sense of meaning sense of fulfillment. We wanted to capture users' mind share. Analogy would be potato chips versus main course. It's different needs under different scenario.

Juliet Yang: So fundamentally, it's two different racetrack. For the short video content, it's a competition for attention. In order to capture users' attention, the platform needs to stimulate and stimulate different type of leading content in order to capture users' attention. As for Bilibili, what we are fighting for is to increase the quality of the content, fighting for users' intentional time spent, making users like us, remember us and wanted to actively explore content and stay with us. There might be some overlaps in terms of demographics, but fundamentally, it's 2 different type of means. And Bilibili represents the longevity and the beautiful side of the community.

If you believe in people will essentially create for high-quality content, they essentially will create for content that brings them meaning purpose and sense of fulfillment, then Bilibili will eventually win over the race in the longer term.

Juliet Yang: We constantly conduct user research and interviews. We found many of Bilibili users they do not spend time on short content because for them, they have very diverse interest. As they grow with us, they would have more desire and demand for high-quality content, and that will keep Bilibili continues to grow.

Juliet Yang: And the second point is the community. Community is Bilibili's strongest specialty as well as -- it is our deepest moat. For community, there are 3 components. #1 would be the users. Bilibili users are probably the most young, energetic demographic on Internet who received good education. They have their own interest world. They pursue high-quality content and they have the ability to appreciate and admire good content. The desire for content that brings some sense of fulfillment. That is Bilibili's core demographic.

Juliet Yang: And the second component is our content creators, and they are from our users. They're young, they have a strong desire to self-express and they are truly talented. Juliet Yang: Lastly, I want to talk about AI. Bilibili is the platform that is the most benefited by the AI's development because our business model is essentially supply driven. AI is unlocking the production of high-quality content, and that is helping us to largely release or solve the supply problem of the high-quality content aspect.

Juliet Yang: AI is helping creators to unlock their productivity. And secondly, AI is helping our algorithm to become smarter to connect better with the great content with the user who are interested.

Juliet Yang: In our earnings, the record high DAU time spent, daily video submission and our average creator income result are largely driven by the AI help.

Juliet Yang: To summarize, we believe our business model is very organic and self-sustaining, and we are one of the very few players who doesn't compete head-to-head with the short content. That is why we remain very confident that Bilibili can continue to deliver healthy and quality growth over time.

Operator: Next, we have Kenneth Fong from UBS.

Kenneth Fong: [Foreign Language] Congrats on the solid quarter. I have a question regarding the advertising business. External macro conditions as well as the overall consumption are likely to remain challenging. Can management share outlook on the advertising business for fourth quarter and next year? I also have a few specific questions like which industry have demand more significantly affected by the macro environment? How do you view the sustainability on AI-related advertising budget growth? Which verticals do you see or do you expect to be the key drivers for advertising growth going forward? And looking further ahead into next year and medium and longer term, where will be the main growth space for Bilibili advertising business coming from?

And how should we think about the growth driver?

Juliet Yang: Thanks for your question. In the second half of the year, we've seen pressure on the macro and consumer overall sentiment. Advertisers are becoming more cautious with their budget, moving away from broad-based spending and looking for more predictable returns. And Bilibili has a unique mind share among young people and our high-quality content drives higher-quality conversions. So much of our growth in the second half comes from a structural shift in advertising budgets within our advertising -- with our advertising revenue growing 20% year-over-year in Q3, and we continue to gain a greater share of advertisers' budget.

Juliet Yang: As for the AI-related advertising spending in Q3, it grew by 95% year-over-year, and we continue to see AI as a reliable source of advertising revenue over mid- to long term. Competition is fierce across both AI infrastructure and application. Unlike in the mobile Internet era, the players in the AI are changing much faster. And advertiser with a substantial budget this quarter may not have the same budget next quarter. But even as the industry goes through rounds of reshuffling and budget allocation, we stand to benefit that is because Bilibili occupies a very unique position in users' mind share when it comes to product reviews, technology content and learning. We are the largest video platform for AI-related knowledge.

Both video views and watch time for AI-related content doubled year-over-year in Q3, while video submission in this category grew over 160% year-over-year. We expect growth in AI-related advertising budget will naturally moderate as the base gets larger. But what won't change is that AI will remain an important structural growth driver for delivery advertising revenue.

Juliet Yang: Our top 5 advertising verticals were in Q3 were games, Internet services, digital products and home appliances, automotive and e-commerce. Beyond AI, advertising revenue from home decoration as well as footwear and apparel grew by 51% and 40% year-over-year, respectively, while education grew over 29%. The growing purchasing power and consumer demand of our users are increasingly translating to advertising revenue.

Juliet Yang: As for the growth driver for our future advertising revenue, first, we benefit from our user growing up with Bilibili. The high-quality content in our community also plays a significant role in shaping users' purchasing decisions. They go from being students to entering the workforce, starting families, buying homes and cars and raising children, their disposable income grows, and they are making increasingly significant purchasing decisions. The 12-month retention rate of our official members has remained around 80% for 10 consecutive years. As the same user move through different stages of life, we are able to benefit from their growing spending power and increasing demand for higher ticket items. That will be our most fundamental growth driver.

Juliet Yang: Secondly, we are expanding across more streams and scenarios, which opens up more advertising inventory. In Q3, advertising revenue from search grew over 50% year-over-year. Next year, we'll continue to explore more ways to monetize the time users spend on our platform.

Juliet Yang: Lastly, I hope AI will further improve our advertising efficiency in several ways. First, AI helps us to better understand content and user needs, allowing us to match ads with the right audiences more efficiently and accurately. AIGC ad creatives and smart campaign management can lower the barriers for producing ad materials and helping new advertisers to overcome the cold start challenges. With the same amount of traffic, we can deliver higher ROIs for our advertisers. This will be particularly important in a softer consumer environment.

Juliet Yang: So looking ahead to Q4 and next year, we are confident that we can continue to outgrow the industry and maintain a healthy, steady growth.

Operator: Next, we have Qi (Daniel) Chen from JPMorgan.

Qi (Daniel) Chen: [Foreign Language] I would translate myself. My question is related to the online game business. So several questions. First one, regarding the Lumi Master, the new game we launched in the fourth quarter, could management share the latest performance after the launch? Also, what's our future plan for this game? And we are also launching another new game at the end of this year, Sanwang. What's the latest test result or the kind of testing feedback from the gamers? Also, how should we expect the revenue performance for the game after its official launch? So from the total number of game pipelines, we can see that 2027, there will be quite a lot of new games launching.

So how should we expect the game performance, the game revenue, game segment performance for 2027? Also within these new games, which are the most -- which one do management think has the biggest potential? And what's the launch timing for these new games?

Juliet Yang: Interpreted Let me start with Lumi Master, our very first self-developed casual creator collecting game. We launched this game globally on September 17. And right now, we also launched via WeChat Mini Game platform to reach a broader group of casual users. In terms of its performance and revenue, it has been in line with what we have expected from a new casual title. It has reached #2 on China's iOS top downloading chart following its launch and overseas performance has also been strong, accounting for about 45% of the game's total gross revenue at the end of October.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted As for the future performances, we will continue to roll out seasonal updates, introducing new content for each season. The biggest expectation for this game is to maintain a healthy and long-term operation. We expect this game to generate positive profit next year, and we will continue to roll out new game content and new IP. And because this is our very first self-developed casual game, we do hope the team will work to innovate -- to provide innovative game experience and continue to convert more users.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted The next project is Sanwang, San Guo Zhi: Wang Dao Tian Xia, which is scheduled to launch on December 24 this year.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted And for Sanwang, this game is officially licensed from the original KOEI Three Kingdoms IP and the art graphics and the characters are very original and are designed for players who have a strong connection to the IP and enjoys the strategy gameplay.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted And the second selling point for this game is that for Sanwang, this game is a deeper strategy game. And compared to our previous strategy game, Sanmo, which is designed to attract younger demographics, lighter gameplay, Sanwang is designed for users that has deeper desire for deep strategy game. They are more senior. They appreciate the IP, and they also have higher spendable income. So the design of these 2 games are to further penetrate the large strategy game market that both of the title also complement each other.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted Our target is that both of the game will attract different group of demographics and it can achieve long-term operation and convert different type of cohort on their own gameplay.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted As for next year, as a matter of fact, the pipeline will be much more robust compared to what we had this year.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted We have 3 new games scheduled for next year. And the first one is RO3, which is a very classic IP with a long-standing history. For this game, it already has secured its publication license, and we've already completed its first technical test in China, and the user feedback has been very enthusiastic.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted The second pipeline is a very typical game that Bilibili user would appreciate. It's called Mistbound, Guild Wars Card Game. It is a very innovative card battling title based on the Guild Wars IP.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted And from the beta testing that we have conducted, the player feedback has been very positive. We are targeting to launch this game in the second half of 2027.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted The third title is our self-development title, Three Kingdoms: The Ravages of Time, which is a tactical strategy RPG.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted This title is adapted from a very classic manga IP, and Bilibili has also published its own cartoons.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted For users that's interested in the tactical card gameplay genre, this would be quite a title to watch out for. And we've conducted beta testing among the core users and the feedback has been positive, and we are also aiming to launch this title next year.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted Among all the title mentioned, we believe Sanwang and RO3 are the 2 most important titles for us.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted Beyond the pipelines, we wanted to focus on the long-term operation of all the titles. We wanted to keep our existing game healthy and sustainable over a very long period of time. Sanmo, which already celebrated its second-year anniversary, FGO, Azur Lane have also maintained steady performances for almost 10 years. So as we launch new games, we're also hoping our existing pool will continue to thrive and all the titles that we publish, we also achieve a long-term operation.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted With the nice addition of our new pipeline, we do believe next year, our game revenue will be much more improved compared to this year.

Operator: Next, we have Xueqing Zhang from CICC.

Xueqing Zhang: [Foreign Language] My question is about AI. You mentioned earlier that AI is having a positive impact on content creation, understanding and distribution. Could management share some specific examples of the progress we have made? Looking ahead to 2027, what are the company's plans for AI investment and what will be the key areas of focus? And also, what level of AI spending should we expect over the next few years? And how might this affect your income statement and cash flow?

Juliet Yang: Interpreted Our investment on AI will be laser-focused. To summarize, we'll use AI on only 1 area, which is the video area.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted So I believe the generative AI for video business is a huge progress. We've witnessed many iteration and innovation in the video landscape from movie to TV to online videos. We believe that generative AI for videos, the benefit and the progress it brings will be larger than in the history combined.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted We believe AI will increase the industry value by 10x. That's a huge opportunity for Bilibili. That is why I also spent quite some time on how AI can help make Bilibili better.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted We are focusing on AI on 3 different aspects. One is on the consumption area. AI is significantly boosting the efficiency of our recommending algorithm as well as our search function. In the generative AI era, it has increased 100x efficiency in terms of understanding the content itself and match better content with the users' intent and interest. That is significantly boosting the efficiency of our algorithm at the same time, improve user experience.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted So the DAU, the time spent as well as many metrics across our community are exactly benefiting from the AI adoption into our search and recommendation.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted The second thing is for community. In the AI era, our most valuable moat lies in the vast amount of genuine user interactions and relationship within our community. And in the past time, we've collected many data, but we don't have the ability to fully utilize those user interactions and their labels and preferences. With the help of AI, we can fully unleash that value in the data set.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted In the AI terms is that the user interactions are basically user helping us to label the content and also it reflects user intent and interest, helping us to understand our users much better in a different level.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted The last aspect is on the creative tools. We see that a good AI creation tools is helping us to increase the supply as well as the quality of great content in a much bigger level.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted We've already launched 2 AI creation tools, UpDream and Huasheng, for our creators. We've noticed that this tool is unleashing so much creativity for our creators on a different scale and a different level compared to the simple editing apps.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted Take UpDream, for example, which we launched in April this year. We've already seen videos made with UpDream has already generated over 5 billion minutes of watch time and more than 1,000 of those videos have reached over 1 million views each.

Juliet Yang: Interpreted So fundamentally, our AI investment will be super focused. We will leverage AI to make a better Bilibili. And we hope every money we spend on improving AI will essentially reflect it in our community and our financial performance.

Xin Fan: This is Sam. I will add some color about the financials. To support the training and inference need for our core recommendation updates and creator tools, as mentioned by Rui Chen, we are making some forward-looking investment and building capacity in computing infrastructure depending on market conditions. That said, everything comes down to pricing and terms. We remain strictly disciplined on spending, keeping a close eye on the profitability as well as positive free cash flow. Our overall pace will be prudent and well within our financial capacity. Regarding to the financial impact in next year, that will be largely depend on what we learned from our early exploration and testing.

Some of these investments are one-off, short term and conditional. So if we make more concrete progress, we will share updates in future quarterly discussions. We are maintaining our expectation for full year 2026 non-GAAP operating profit of nearly around RMB 2.8 billion, up around 14% to 15% year-over-year. We are also very confident in our business development progress, and we expect our free cash flow in 2027 will be higher than 2026.

Operator: Next, we have Alex Liu from Bank of America.

Alex Liu: [Foreign Language] My first question is about margin and profitability. So we do observe in the past few years, there has been a very rapid increase of gross margin and general profitability. So wondering how does the management think about the profitability in the next few quarters? And also, I think in September, there has been multiple transactions that -- from the company that has been eliminating the risk of some shareholder share selling and also the company finished a buyback. So on capital allocation, any thoughts or colors that management can share?

Xin Fan: Okay. I will take this question. Our financial performance remained solid in Q3. Revenue grew 8% year-over-year and gross margin further improved to 37.3%. We continue to see operating leverage with operating profit growing 32% year-over-year and adjusted operating profit growing 17% year-over-year. Our adjusted operating margin improved from 9% a year ago to 9.7% right now and adjusted net profit margin reached 10%. Looking ahead to Q4, we expect our adjusted operating margin to be in the high single digits, and the gross profit margin will be flat quarter-over-quarter. We are maintaining our expectation for full year profit to nearly RMB 2.8 billion and representing a growth rate around 15%.

And regarding to the capital allocation, in our recent concurrent share buyback project, since September 2026, we have repurchased a total of USD 300 million shares, all of which have been canceled. This reduced our total outstanding shares by approximately 4.9%, which will help improve our EPS. Apart from these special repurchases, we have another USD 300 million share repurchase program approved by our Board in June. We also repurchased USD 15 million worth of shares this quarter with opportunately, we still have USD 250 million remaining under the program. We have ample share cash reserves with over RMB 25 billion in cash and cash equivalents at the end of Q3.

We will continue to repurchase shares at opportunities and deliver sustainable long-term returns to our shareholders.

Juliet Yang: Thank you, operator. That will be our last question.

Operator: And that concludes the Q&A session. Thank you once again for joining Bilibili's Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Business Update Conference Call today. If you have any further questions, please contact Juliet Yang, Bilibili Executive IR Director or Piacente Financial Communications. Contact information for IR in both China and the U.S. can be found on today's press release. Thank you, and have a great day.

#3091. You can now DM Meta’s Muse on Instagram to turn saves into plans

Meta's personal AI agent now takes requests in Instagram's inbox, starting with the posts you have saved.

Meta has added its Muse AI agent to Instagram direct messages, inviting users to send it a DM to turn saved posts into plans, such as a trip. Muse already worked in its own app, in WhatsApp and on Instagram profiles, and Meta says it does not read private messages unless users allow it, though Reuters reported staff found it reading encrypted chats.

Meta’s Muse AI agent can now be messaged in Instagram DMs, where it can turn posts users have saved into plans. Meta announced the change through Muse’s own Instagram account on Tuesday, using a long-planned trip as the example.

Muse launched in the US in September as an agent that books, buys and negotiates for users. It works in its own app and in WhatsApp, and later that month users could add it to their Instagram profiles.

The DM option puts Muse where the saved posts already sit. Meta has not said which countries get it. Beyond the US, Muse is live in Canada and has launched in Australia, and it reached the UK this week.

Yet Reuters reported last week that Meta staff found Muse reading encrypted messages. Meta called those isolated incidents.

Users can also make Muse ask before it sends messages or buys anything. In September, though, a YouTuber said Muse shared his address with a Facebook Marketplace buyer before asking him. Meta said it was looking into it.

#3090. GTA 6 is a generational masterpiece — and one of the few games I’ve given a perfect score in 16 years

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Unlock and manage exclusive Tom’s Guide member rewards.

Join the Tom's Guide Club for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6 is easily the most impressive entry in the (in)famous series and a technical showcase that raises the bar for open-world games. Its expansive map and myriad activities offer countless hours of crime-fueled mayhem, while the intriguing characters keep you invested in the narrative. This game was worth the wait and will arguably go down as the finest title of this console generation.

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Platforms: PS5 (reviewed), Xbox Series X/SPrice: $79 / £69 / AU$129Release date: November 19, 2026Genre: Open-world action-adventure

GTA 6 is the most impressive video game I’ve ever played. I’m not surprised, given Rockstar Games’ history of releasing technically proficient (and insanely profitable) titles, but the storied developers have truly outdone most other games with what they’ve accomplished here. The long wait and anticipation are more than justified.

Larger than any locale in the franchise’s history, the fictional state of Leonida is a character unto itself, evoking real-life Florida with its myriad eccentric characters and diverse locations. You explore this vast landscape alongside the game’s two protagonists, a Bonnie-and-Clyde-like couple who help keep the emotional center in place amid the chaos of the main story and side quests. Together, the narrative and open-world elements deliver an experience that keeps you hooked for hours.

I’ve been a huge fan of the GTA series since GTA 3 arrived in 2001 and completely changed the gaming landscape. I had some trepidation about GTA 6, given how long we’ve waited for it and how much gaming (and the world) has changed since GTA 5was released in 2013. Thankfully, GTA 6 far exceeds my expectations and will more than likely be my favorite game of the generation. Here’s why...

GTA 6 straddles the line between the more grounded tone of GTA 4 and the over-the-top insanity of GTA 5. It’s fair to say this game feels like Red Dead Redemption 2 set in the 21st century, in both tone and theme. Given that RDR 2 is in my top 10 favorite games of all time, this is a major bonus.

That Red Dead inspiration is most evident in the game’s first chapter, where we slowly learn about the two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, a criminal couple trying to build a new life. The slower-burn intro will turn off anyone who's played the arcade-y GTA Online for the past 13 years—and it’s a valid criticism, even if I personally didn’t mind it. After chapter 1, it’s full-on GTA-style mayhem.

Jason and Lucia have more grounded personalities than some of the wilder protagonists in older GTA titles, but the game generally does a good job of showing what motivates them and making you feel invested in their journey. Jason and Lucia balance each other, with the former more stoic and calculated and the latter more impulsive and instinctive. The characters are at their best together and feel incomplete apart. The leads’ relatively toned-down attitudes also contrast nicely with the absolutely bonkers characters they meet along the way.

In true GTA fashion, this is a rags-to-riches criminal tale that builds with each subsequent mission. You feel the sense of progression as you move up in the world and take on bigger, more dangerous heists. Watching the protagonists evolve over the course of the story is also satisfying.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

In the Grand Theft Auto series, driving has often been a point of contention, and that hasn’t changed here. At least initially. During the first few hours, I found the driving mechanics overly sensitive and loose. It felt like I was driving on ice, especially in the beat-up jalopy Jason owns at the beginning.

Then I realized that, at least on PS5, the triggers are pressure-sensitive, and I shouldn’t just hold R2 all the way down. In fact, you can feel a bit of resistance when you depress the button halfway. When I figured this out, I was golden. Though some vehicles naturally control better and differently than others, I now have a good handle (no pun intended) on the pretty intricate driving mechanics.

Pay & Spray shops are not only great for a quick paint job to lose the cops, but also for tuning your car’s performance for better handling. This can be expensive, so it’s best to wait until you have enough money and a car worth investing in, since you don’t want to upgrade a piece of crap. I like tuning cars because it reminds me of Rockstar’s Midnight Club racing series. And yes, you can totally add neon lights and nitrous!

Stealing cars is more involved than ever. While you can easily steal most cheaper or older cars, higher-end vehicles will have alarms, key fobs, and trackers. And even when you successfully jack a car, you need to hotwire it. The game doles out specific tools needed to steal various cars at specific points, so you'll need to be patient to grab the really high-end rides. Even if jacking cars requires more than a button press, the extra steps make stealing them feel more immersive.

As criminals, Jason and Lucia always end up getting into gunfights—either with fellow lawbreakers or law enforcement. Though the shooting and cover mechanics aren’t as precise and responsive as a dedicated third-person shooter like Gears of War: E-Day, they’re the most refined of any previous GTA game.

Auto lock for weapons was essential in GTA 5 and RDR 2 because the free-aiming mechanics were so dodgy and imprecise. That’s not the case here, as I can easily land headshots with auto lock disabled. This game has its own version of Red Dead’s “Dead Eye,” called Focus Mode, which slows the world down so you can target specific body parts. This is crucial if you want to shoot arms or legs to disable rather than kill, especially since it ties into the game’s morality system. Jason and Lucia both have a Focus meter that drains while you’re in Focus Mode.

The cover mechanics are good but not great. I say that because while your character sticks to walls or the sides of cars you’re hiding behind, it’s too easy to snap out of cover when you try to move. Still, the mechanic works well enough most of the time, and you definitely want to stay in cover during intense shootouts with gang members or the police.

You have access to all manner of handguns, shotguns, assault rifles, and more, which you can purchase from Ammu-Nation, pilfer from dispatched enemies, or find in the open world. Like cars, you can modify weapons. Of course, buying upgrades that improve handling, extend magazine capacity, add scopes, and more can get expensive, but it’s well worth it given the number of insane shootouts you’ll encounter during the story or out in Leonidas.

Sticking up pawn shops and robbing banks has always been fun in GTA, but it’s even more enjoyable now with two protagonists. I never get tired of watching how shop owners and customers react when Jason and Lucia bust in with guns drawn. While one makes sure no one tries anything funny, the other threatens the clerk into emptying the register. Sometimes someone tries to be a hero and stop you, so you have to stay on your guard.

That scenario is for small shops, but if you want to break into a bank, you’ll need to prepare. Scoping out a place, either from the inside or outside, to locate exits and where the goods are kept is crucial to pulling off a successful heist. And don’t forget to have a getaway vehicle nearby, as the cops will arrive quickly if alarms are triggered (though you can always try to disable them).

Along the way, you’ll also discover or be told where gangs hang out or where other criminal activity occurs. These locations often have jewelry, drugs, or other contraband that you can then sell to a fence for a big haul. As with bank robberies, you’ll want to scope out a location to identify entry points and other opportunities to exploit.

The wanted system is more intricate than before. Committing crimes in a specific area raises your wanted level by up to six stars, with each star bringing more heat from law enforcement. You can drive to another county to lose the heat, but the cops will remember your vehicle, face, hairstyle, clothing, and that there were two of you. To really lose the cops, you’ll need to change your clothes, repaint your car, or temporarily split up.

For example, I got a 4-star wanted rating after a robbery went wrong. I drove my car deep into the woods and got out, using the trees for cover to avoid being spotted by helicopters. After finding a truck depot, I broke into a truck using a slim jim carjacking tool and stayed in the truck without turning it on. The cops swarmed the area but didn’t find me because I was lying low. After a few minutes, they left, and I drove off to change clothes and switch vehicles. None of this was scripted.

Since this is a crime game, I’m glad Rockstar updated the wanted system to feel more realistic and give you the freedom to evade the fuzz in ways not available in previous titles.

Now, I won’t go into exhaustive detail about all the side activities available. Suffice it to say that if you need a break from your criminal pursuits, there is plenty to do. That said, I want to discuss some of my favorites.

Like in previous games, you can do side missions for some of the zany characters you meet. I enjoy these because they are small stories unto themselves, and also let you experience more of Leonidas’ environment and cultures. No spoilers here, but some of these side missions are completely bonkers, and sometimes quite literally out of this world.

This may sound weird, given how I neglect to do this in real life, but I’m obsessed with taking Jason and Lucia to the gym. And it’s not just because I want them to look buff and hot. For instance, lifting weights boosts your strength, making you a bit harder to kill and letting you punch enemies out more easily. Boosting your cardio lets you run and swim longer, while raising your Focus can extend your Focus Mode. You can also boost these stats by brawling, running, or eating, but I find hitting the gym more efficient and fun.

You’ll also find several events that lead to missions not marked on the map. For example, you might return to your car only to find a random woman in the backseat asking for help retrieving her dog from a biker gang, or an influencer might decide to snap photos of herself with your fancy ride. This is why it pays to explore methodically, as surprises are literally around every corner.

Among other things, you can participate in street or boat races, get drunk and blow all your money at strip clubs, do some mud wrestling, or unwind by watching TV (the in-game TV shows are hilarious) or doomscrolling on your phone with your partner in bed after a long day of chaos. There is no shortage of interesting activities to partake in here.

I say this without a hint of hyperbole, but GTA 6 is the most graphically impressive and detailed game I’ve ever seen. Rockstar’s proprietary RAGE Engine is in full effect, delivering awe-inspiring visuals that bring Leonida to life. Videos online can’t compare to the experience of playing GTA 6 firsthand.

The map is immense. Even at full speed on the highway, it can take five or more minutes to reach a destination. And you won’t even mind, since everything you pass is so wonderfully rendered, from distant bridges to forests beneath thick, darkening clouds. I especially love driving through Vice City at night, as the metropolis’ gleaming buildings and neon-drenched streets are a sight to behold.

Since Leonida is essentially a miniature version of Florida, it has similar biomes. These include muggy swamps, dense woods, and the terrifying marvel of the Caribbean Sea. As in RDR 2, the world is filled with all manner of animals, from small rats to enormous sperm whales. You can easily spend hours exploring each locale, as long as you’re wary of hungry alligators or sharks.

Humans are as intricately detailed as the animals and environments. During my playthrough, I didn’t see a single NPC who resembled another. I’m also impressed that certain character types appear only in specific neighborhoods, which adds to the realism. You can spend all day people-gazing, as the fine folks of Leonidas always have something interesting to say. But as with exploring the wilds, keep a weapon handy for when someone inevitably tries to mug you.

I played on a PS5 Pro, which, like all consoles that GTA 6 is available on, is capped at 30 frames per second. During my time, I never once saw the frame rate dip, even during intense shootouts or fast-moving chase sequences. Naturally, your experience may differ, even if you’re also playing on a PS5 Pro, but I never encountered performance issues. And though I wish we could have gotten at least 40 fps on the PS5 Pro, the locked 30 fps runs as smoothly as possible.

Beyond the gorgeous visuals, the GTA 6 experience isn’t complete without its incredible soundtrack. With over 22 radio stations featuring dozens of songs, there’s no shortage of awesome tracks to play while you commit crimes.

As before, you get a nice mix of stations featuring contemporary and classic tunes. There are also a handful of talk radio stations, which have always been a favorite of mine. Every station has an eclectic DJ or two to keep things lively. The radio stations also round out the world of GTA 6, offering entertaining insights on celebrities, famous establishments, current news, and more.

The original tunes are just as nice as the expansive licensed soundtrack. You mostly hear this music during cinematic scenes, but it also pops up when you’re fleeing the cops. There’s also a particular track from rap duo Bau-Luxe that will have you laughing out loud because of its obscene lyrics that I won’t even hint at here!

This has been one of my longer game reviews, and even it only scratches the surface of the GTA 6 experience. Suffice it to say, you can (and some will) sink countless hours into this world and still not see everything Rockstar managed to cram into it. Like an expensive drink you can buy in Vice City, this is a title you’ll want to savor, not rush.

GTA 6 is everything we could have hoped for and more. Despite a few minor quibbles, nothing here detracts significantly. I’ve never given a game I’ve reviewed at Tom’s Guide a full five stars, but if any game deserves that honor, it’s certainly GTA 6. It’s a once-in-a-generation title that shows what’s possible when you give a talented team the budget and time to craft something exceptional. GTA 6 really is that damn good!

#3089. iPhone Handoff: Here’s the latest on carrier availability and pricing

iPhone Handoff is a new feature in iOS 27 that lets you use the same phone number across two different iPhones. However, the feature requires carrier support, so it isn’t available to everyone. Here are the carriers that currently support iPhone Handoff and those that have promised support.

9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off. These deliver immersive 360 Spatial Sound, active noise canceling, low-latency wireless connectivity, and much more.

With iPhone Handoff, you can use the same phone number on two different iPhones. Your number automatically moves between the two phones, depending on which one you pick up. This includes calls, voicemail, messages, and Find My location.

Simply unlock whichever device you want to use and you’re ready to go. Other data synced with iCloud will automatically update across your devices. Third-party apps work across both devices, following each app’s own syncing behavior.

iPhone Handoff is available on iOS 27 and later. The phones must be connected to Wi-Fi, share the same Apple Account, use Messages in iCloud, and be signed into FaceTime and iMessage with the same Apple Account.

The biggest limiting factor of iPhone Handoff is that it requires carrier support. Currently, just three carriers support the feature:

What about carriers that are working on the feature? In the United States, Verizon has promised it “will support iPhone Handoff,” but it’s unclear when the feature will launch. Verizon says it will charge $10 per month for the service.

AT&T, meanwhile, has no plans to support iPhone Handoff. In a statement in September, the carrier said that its focus “remains on delivering innovations that make life simpler and keep customers connected with confidence.” The carrier noted that there “could be potential in capabilities like iPhone Handoff,” but that customers should use “existing eSIM activation and transfer options” instead.

No other carriers have promised support for iPhone Handoff, so it’s unclear how quickly the feature will expand around the world.

In my testing, iPhone Handoff works really well. I have it set up between my iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. I use the iPhone Duo 90% of the time, but when I do pick up my iPhone 18 Pro, my number instantly switches to it. There’s a cute animation that expands from the Dynamic Island, confirming that the number has moved.

Have you tried iPhone Handoff? Are you willing to pay extra for it? Let us know down in the comments.

#3088. Muse safety debate continues as the AI agent rolls out in the UK

The debate over the wisdom and safety of using Meta’s Muse AI agent continues as the app rolls out in the UK. It follows a warning by a number of regulatory bodies about the potential risks of AI agents …

Meta yesterday announced the UK availability of Muse.

Muse, Meta’s personal Al agent, is now available to adults in the UK. Think of it as a helping hand for the jobs that pile up, like chasing a refund, renewing car insurance or keeping on top of the school calendar. To get those jobs done you can connect Muse to the apps you already use, from your email and calendar to the retailer apps you shop on.

A forum representing four different UK regulatory bodies last month issued a warning about the potential dangers involved in using AI agents. The Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum said:

AI agents may amplify and accelerate risks and introduce new ones. These risks may increase as the capabilities of personal agents grow and adoption rises. Questions of consumer protection, competition and data protection – for example the risk of fraud and scams, personal information sharing not in line with user expectations and misleading recommendations, decisions or information provided – must be addressed to ensure innovation develops in ways that earn and maintain public trust.

Meta has pushed back against suggestions that Muse has accessed personal data without permission, insisting that users are in control and must approve important actions. The company has admitted to some “isolated incidents,” but says other reported breaches were either hallucinations or took place on internal versions of the app while undergoing testing. In a new blog post, Meta says:

Muse only works with the apps and services you choose to connect it to, and you control the access it gets […] Once you’ve decided what Muse is connected to and what you want it to do, with your oversight, it can handle tasks like searching, comparing and planning for you. But before it does anything like sending an email or buying something, it shows you exactly what it’s about to do and waits for your go-ahead. A separate security agent checks Muse’s actions and the information it sends out against the permissions you’ve granted. You can also choose how often it checks in with you in Settings.

At the time of writing, Muse remains the second most popular free app in Apple’s US App Store, with more than 10 million downloads. We reported yesterday that some banks are already blocking AI agents, while others are warning that they will not be responsible for the consequences of any actions taken by them.

#3087. Anthropic lets MCP servers ship skills and run background jobs in Claude

Shopify, GitHub and Supabase are among the first to use the new features in Claude and Claude Code.

Anthropic has opened Skills over MCP in public beta, letting apps that connect to Claude ship playbooks alongside their tools. Tasks, for long background jobs, and Elicitation, which pauses for user input, are now generally available, with File Uploads coming soon.

Apps that plug into Claude through MCP can now also tell it how to use them, Anthropic said on Tuesday. The feature, Skills over MCP, is in public beta in Claude and Claude Code.

MCP is the open standard Anthropic launched two years ago to link AI agents to outside apps and data. Servers built on it already list the tools Claude can use. With skills, they can also ship step-by-step guides and best practices, which Claude loads only when needed.

Shopify uses skills to help Claude design and update online stores, and HubSpot to onboard customers. Skills update with the server, so users have nothing extra to install. More apps are opening up, too: Canva opened its MCP server to all developers on Tuesday.

The beta is on by default for Pro, Max and Ultra plans. Team admins can switch it on, and Enterprise support is coming soon.

Two other features are now generally available. Tasks lets a server run long jobs in the background while Claude keeps working, which ZoomInfo uses for deeper research. Elicitation lets a server pause and ask the user for input.

GitHub, for example, makes users type a repository’s name before an agent deletes it. Supabase confirms costs before creating a paid project. A fourth feature, File Uploads, will soon let Claude send PDFs, spreadsheets and images to servers.

The features are part of MCP, so servers that support them also work in other compatible apps. Anthropic says MCP now sees over 700M SDK downloads a month. In August, OpenAI and four rivals agreed on a standard for packaging skills and MCP servers.

Skills carry risks, too. That same month, researchers found malicious agent skills that stole passwords and keys after about 1.7 million installs.

#3086. iOS 27 breaks 15 years of muscle memory on iPhone and iPad

Since iOS 5 in 2011, the iPhone and iPad have included Notification Center, a central place to find alerts from various apps in chronological order.

Starting with iOS 27, Apple is making a major change to how users open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.

iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases. The behavior changed slightly between the first two releases. However, this change shipped, and I’m still adjusting to it.

Opening Notification Center is unchanged on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 by default. However, enabling Siri AI changes a key swipe gesture on both iPhone and iPad.

One of the many ways of invoking Siri AI, once enabled, is by swiping down from the center of the top edge of your iPhone or iPad display. This previously opened Notification Center.

You can still access Notification Center by swiping down from the top-left corner once Siri AI is enabled. Alerts now animate in from the top left corner. This is a way to point users toward Notification Center’s smaller surface area.

Apple is greatly prioritizing Siri AI access in iOS 27. The majority of the top edge is devoted to invoking the new Siri experience.

The last time Apple made a change to accessing Notification Center came when Control Center moved from a swipe up gesture from the bottom to a top-right corner swipe down gesture on iPhone X. Apple later unified this experience across devices.

Now it’s Notification Center’s turn to be put in the corner. On iPadOS 27 beta 1 in particular, the area above Home screen app icons was pretty much devoted to invoking Siri AI. The area for opening Notification Center actually shrank if you disable displaying AM/PM or the date.

I've been always swiping from the left corner to see my notifications. I didn't even know you could swipe from the center to get to it as well 😂 I guess I'm good then?

Apple improved this with iPadOS 27 beta 2, creating a more uniform region on either side. It’s roughly the size of two app columns with Notification Center on the left and Control Center on the right. The rest is for invoking Siri.

After 15 years of muscle memory, it’ll take some time to determine if this change is worth it or something that should be reconsidered. In the meantime, early feedback sounds overwhelmingly positive around Apple’s new Siri AI system. Hearing that Siri is good now will also take some getting used to, I’m sure.

After months of using the new behavior, I’m certain I’d toggle it off if there were a setting to do so. Since there’s no option to disable invoking Siri from the top middle swipe down, the only thing to do is build new muscle memory around avoiding the center.

What do you think? Would you change this back if you could? Is accessing Siri from the swipe-down gesture worth the change? Share your thoughts in the comments.
