#3079. BingEx (FLX) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Revenue slipped as delivery rivals intensified, but AI now handles 90% of service cases.

By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 24, 2026 at 2:57PM EST

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

BingEx (FLX -1.99%) reported a year-over-year decline in total revenue as competition in the Chinese on-demand delivery market intensified. Management maintained a stable gross margin through optimized merchant acquisition and disciplined spending while significantly expanding the role of artificial intelligence across research and operational functions. The company launched a new service category for everyday assistance and deepened integrations with major platform ecosystems to diversify user acquisition channels. Strategic focus remained on high-value delivery segments and improving the fulfillment capacity of the courier network while executing a multi-million dollar share repurchase program.

Operator: Good day, and welcome to BingEx' 2026 Third Quarter Financial Results Conference Call. Today's conference is being recorded. At this time, I would like to turn the conference over to Helen Wu from Piacente Financial Communications. Please go ahead.

Helen Wu: Thank you, operator. During this call, we will discuss our business outlook and make forward-looking statements. These comments are based on our predictions and expectations as of today. Actual events or results could differ materially from those mentioned in today's news release and in this discussion due to a number of risks and uncertainties, including those mentioned in our most recent filings with the SEC. The non-GAAP financial measures we provide are for comparison purpose only. The definition of these measures and a reconciliation table are available in the news release we issued earlier today. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

In addition, a webcast replay of this conference call will be available on the BingEx company's IR website at ir.ishansong.com. Furthermore, throughout the call, we will constantly use the company brand name FlashEx to refer to its publicly listed entity, BingEx Limited. Joining us today from FlashEx senior management are Mr. Adam Xue, Founder, Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer; Mr. Hongjian Yu, Co-Founder, Director and Executive President; and Mr. Luke Tang, Chief Financial Officer. I will now turn the call over to Mr. Adam Xue.

Peng (Adam) Xue: Thank you, Helen. Hello, everyone, and welcome to FlashEx's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. Competition in the on-demand delivery industry remained intense in the third quarter, responded by sharpening our execution and strengthening our differentiated on-demand dedicated courier model. We improved user acquisition efficiency, our merchant mix and fulfillment experience while also expanding into new scenarios and new cities at a measured pace. Doing this work well is what positions FlashEx for long-term growth. Let me start with our overall operations. We fulfilled 62.8 million orders in the third quarter, largely in line with the second quarter and average delivery time held steady at around 25.3 minutes.

As of the end of the third quarter, our registered users increased to 128 million, registered Flash Riders rose to 3.33 million and our service network expanded to 301 cities. As we keep growing our user base and delivery capacity, we are focusing more on turning these resources into reliable service capabilities while steadily improving operating efficiency. Turning to our financial performance. Total revenues for the third quarter were RMB 929.4 million with a gross margin of 11.2%. Non-GAAP income from operations was RMB 16.1 million. As of the end of the third quarter, our cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments totaled RMB 816.4 million, reflecting a healthy financial position.

We also remained committed to enhancing shareholder returns through share repurchases. As of November 23, we had repurchased a total of approximately 4.9 million ADS for an aggregate consideration of approximately USD 13.3 million. Now let me walk through our business in more detail. On the individual user side, we prioritize acquisition efficiency and the conversion of new users. We concentrated our marketing spend on higher converting channels in the third quarter, lowering new user acquisition cost by more than 30% quarter-over-quarter. First order conversion and order volume from new users both increased. Beyond our own channels, we are also reaching users by integrating our services into the ecosystem of major platforms.

Orders through our Quick Apps in the Huawei HarmonyOS ecosystem grew 27% quarter-over-quarter. Our partnership with Alipay expanded from assisted purchasing to its lifestyle services channel and users have begun placing orders through the Zhixiaobao AI agent. In terms of use cases, both our core categories and our diverse everyday lifestyle scenarios continued to grow. In cakes, a long-standing core category for us, order volume increased 19% year-over-year in the third quarter. This growth was driven by stronger gifting demand and stable partnerships with leading cake brands, reflecting the trust FlashEx has built with high-quality merchants over the years.

On the everyday side, total order volume across our 5 lifestyle scenarios grew 3.5% quarter-over-quarter, led by food pickup and parcel pickup. These everyday needs also point us in a clear direction for expanding our lifestyle services. With this in mind, we launched our new service, Flash Helper or Flash Assist in the third quarter. It brings the standardized processes and attentive one-on-one service to everyday needs such as waiting in line at restaurants, handling small tasks and moving or carrying items for users. Demand for this kind of assistance has long existed but remains highly fragmented.

Early results show that new users account for high share of Flash Helper orders, making the service an additional channel for expanding our user base and extending user lifetime. We will keep refining the service and use our existing Flash Rider network to explore more services that fit users' daily needs. For users with higher service expectations, we continue to refine our premium delivery service in the third quarter. Premium delivery order volume grew significantly quarter-over-quarter, and the number of new users increased by approximately 37%. This service further diversifies our product tiers, so we can better meet users' varying needs for speed and attention to detail.

On the merchant side, we focused on improving both the quality of our merchant base and our service capabilities while deepening our relationships with existing merchants. We concentrated on raising the quality of newly acquired merchants. To that end, we ran a pilot in 6 cities in northern China, where we optimized resource allocation based on merchants' operating profiles and flexibly adjusted pricing strategies to market conditions in each channel and city, balancing merchant acquisition with ongoing operations. These adjustments are already paying off with gross profit improving in the pilot cities. For our KA business, we moved into a tiered operating model, managing national and regional accounts separately, leveraging the stable high-density order flow from our enterprise clients channels.

We have built a strong delivery competitive base in core business districts, which in turn is driving new merchant acquisition and revenue growth in these areas. In the third quarter, average daily order volume from KA merchants grew quarter-over-quarter, and their share of GMV rose to 17.6%. As the quality of merchant business continues to improve, our business has become even more resilient. For entering new cities and new districts, we adopted a more return-driven expansion model. Our existing teams and our partners run this market directly, drawing on the people and experience we already have to get started quickly with lower upfront investment.

In the third quarter, average daily order volume in newly launched cities and districts rose sharply from the second quarter with some areas turning profitable within a short period. These results provide a proven template for future expansion. Going forward, we will replicate the model progressively, tailoring our approach to local market conditions as we enter new cities. Whether we are serving existing users or developing new services, reliable fulfillment always comes first. In the third quarter, we strengthened our delivery capacity by starting with the Flash Rider experience. We refined our tiered growth framework for Flash Riders with development paths for those riding regularly, those riding flexibly and those building advanced skills.

We also introduced an owner certification that recognizes Flash Riders for strong service and encourage them to keep improving. As Flash Rider income rose steadily, we saw a higher share of regular active Flash Riders and better fulfillment quality with the perfect order rate climbing further and the complaints continue to fall. Order completion rates also improved year-over-year during peak demand periods and in high-density areas such as holidays and core business districts. A stable, well-supported Flash Rider team ultimately translates into a more reliable experience for our users. Yesterday, we celebrated our ninth annual Flash Rider Day together with Flash Riders across the country.

Since we established the day in 2018, we have marked every November 3 by recognizing those who stand out for their professional service and good deeds in the community and by thanking all of our Flash Riders through online and offline events and benefits. Going forward, we will keep investing in safety, skills training, career development and everyday support, creating a better working environment and giving our Flash Riders more room to grow. Our Flash Riders' experience on the road are also helping more users understand the value of FlashEx.

In the third quarter, we built content around real-life Flash Rider stories and expanded our network of around 690 Flash Rider KOLs beyond Beijing to more cities using AI tools to produce and review content more efficiently. For the first time, we also combined a celebrity partnership, holiday timing and a new service in a single campaign, promoting Flash Helper's everyday assistance services during the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays. Our brand communications focus on showing users what FlashEx can do for them in specific real-life situations so that every service experience gradually adds up to trust in our brand.

On the technology front, we continued to put AI into practice to improve efficiency across R&D, customer service and operations. Efficiency gains in these areas increased from 30% in the second quarter to 46% in the third quarter. In R&D, the share of AI-assisted coding exceeded 98%. At the end of September, Super Agent, our self-developed internal development agent, completed its first development tasks end-to-end on its own. Next, we will extend AI further into requirement analysis, testing and release with the goal of shortening development cycles. In customer service, AI has moved beyond standardized Q&A into more open-ended inquiries, now handling close to 90% of cases in core scenarios allow our human agents to concentrate on more complex requests.

In operations, AI tools are increasingly used by our frontline teams. They are gradually moving into a more efficient digital way of working at every level from headquarters to the frontline. Our low-altitude delivery business moved into routine operations in the third quarter. By the end of the quarter, we have built 15 takeoff and landing sites and 24 2-way delivery routes in Hangzhou, covering the city's main districts. Order volume grew 13% quarter-over-quarter. Next, we will focus on 3 areas to further extend the service coverage and capabilities, building a denser network coordinating across channels and partnering with government and other enterprises. Looking ahead, we will focus on improving new users conversion and optimizing our merchant mix.

Building on our existing capabilities, we will also steadily expand our service scenarios and city network. We will also continue to invest in enhancing the experience of both our Flash Riders and our users and deepen the application of AI across our business to deliver better service with greater efficiency. For 12 years, FlashEx has built its business around on-demand dedicated courier services. Our focus has always been the same, providing reliable service the user needed at urgent and important moments. Going forward, with every high-quality delivery and service, we will keep building the trust that the users and merchants place in FlashEx and make that trust the foundation of a long-term sustainable growth. That concludes my remarks.

Now I will turn the call over to our CFO, Luke Tang. Thank you.

Le (Luke) Tang: Thank you, Adam. Hello, everyone. This is Luke. I would like now to walk you through our third quarter 2026 financial results. During the third quarter, our unique on-demand dedicated courier model remained resilient in a competitive market with order volume holding steady quarter-over-quarter. Backed by a disciplined approach to spending and a healthy cash position, we have the flexibility to keep investing in fulfillment quality while exploring new services and use cases. We also remain committed to enhancing shareholder returns through our repurchase program. Before I begin, please note that all numbers are in renminbi and all percentage changes are on year-over-year basis, unless otherwise noted.

Our revenues for the third quarter were RMB 929.4 million compared with RMB 1,005.4 million in the same period of 2025. The decrease was primarily driven by intensifying market competition. Our cost of revenues for the third quarter was RMB 824.8 million compared with RMB 893.6 million in the same period of 2025. The decrease was in line with the decline in revenues. Our gross profit was RMB 104.5 million for the third quarter compared with RMB 111.8 million in the same period of 2025, representing a gross profit margin of 11.2% compared with 11.1% in the same period of 2025. Turning to operating expenses.

Our total operating expenses for the third quarter were RMB 93.5 million, representing a decrease of 4.3% from RMB 97.7 million in the same period of 2025. They consisted of RMB 40.3 million in selling and marketing expenses, RMB 36.6 million in general and administrative expenses and RMB 16.6 million in research and development expenses. The decrease in operating expenses was mainly attributable to the reduction in advertising expenses and share-based compensation expenses. Our income from operations was RMB 11.1 million compared with RMB 14.1 million in the same period of 2025. Excluding share-based compensation expenses, our non-GAAP income from operations was RMB 16.1 million for the third quarter compared with RMB 23.7 million in the same period of 2025.

Our net loss was RMB 6.8 million compared with net income of RMB 43.7 million in the same period of 2025. The change was mainly due to an investment loss of RMB 19.7 million in the third quarter compared with investment income of RMB 33.2 million in the same period of 2025. Excluding changes in fair value of long-term investments and share-based compensation expenses, our non-GAAP net loss was RMB 1 million compared with non-GAAP net income of RMB 62.6 million in the same period of 2025. Our cash position remained healthy with cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments totaling RMB 816.4 million as of the third quarter end.

We also continue to carry out share repurchases under our existing buyback program. As of November 23, we had repurchased a total of approximately 4.9 million ADS in the open market for an aggregate consideration of approximately USD 13.3 million. This underscores our confidence in the company's long-term value. As we close out 2026, we remain committed to disciplined execution and to the high-quality service that differentiates us with a distinctive business model and an improving merchant mix and the deeper use of AI across our operations. We are confident in our ability to create sustainable long-term value for our shareholders. That concludes our prepared remarks. We would like to open the floor to your questions. Operator, please go ahead.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] We will now take our first question. This question comes from the line of [indiscernible] from CICC.

Unknown Analyst: This is [indiscernible] from CICC. Actually, two questions on my side. The first one is about margins and financials. We noticed that our gross margins held up well, yet operating margins compressed. Could you please walk us through what drove the pressures on the OpEx side? And on the non-GAAP net loss swing, how much of that is operating versus below the line items? And my second question is about shareholder returns. You still have about half of the buyback authorization remaining. How should we think about the pace of repurchase going forward, particularly given the current earnings trajectory?

Le (Luke) Tang: Thank you, [indiscernible]. I will take your first question and hand over the second one to Adam. Yes, our gross margin held steady this quarter. So the change in operating margin came mainly from operating expenses due to new initiatives we launched. During the third quarter, we launched Flash Helper, which helps users do everyday tasks such as waiting in line at restaurants or moving or carrying items. And we promoted it with our first celebrity campaign around the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays. So compared with the second quarter, we spent more on marketing to support these launches. We also kept investing in R&D, especially in AI.

We are already using AI tools to create and review marketing content faster. And over time, we expect them to make our marketing spend more efficient. Going forward, we will remain disciplined on overall spending. On a non-GAAP basis, there was a decrease in the fair value of our short-term investments in the third quarter. Our core business stayed profitable with a non-GAAP income from operations of RMB 16.1 million. Yes, I would like to hand over the second question to Adam.

Peng (Adam) Xue: Okay. Thank you, Luke. And also thank you, [indiscernible], for your question. I will answer the second question. Well, our commitment to creating value for shareholders hasn't changed, and that is what guides our buyback program. In terms of progress, as of November 23, we have bought back about 4.9 million ADS for around USD 13.3 million under our USD 30 million program. Buybacks are one of several ways we return value to shareholders. As for the pace from here, we will stay flexible, taking into account market conditions, operating performance and our funding needs and act when the time is right in compliance with applicable SEC rules. Our balance sheet gives us a solid base for this.

We ended the quarter with RMB 816.4 million in cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments. Over the long run, we believe that continuing to strengthen our business, combined with prudent use of share repurchases is the best way to create long-term shareholder value. The buyback program also reflects our confidence in the company's long-term prospects.

Operator: That concludes our Q&A session for today. I will now hand back to Helen Wu for closing remarks.

Helen Wu: Thank you once again for joining BingEx' Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Business Update Conference Call today. If you have any further questions, please contact the IR team at BingEx or Piacente Financial Communications. Thank you and have a great day.

Operator: Thank you. This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.

#3078. iPad Air vs iPad Pro: Which should you buy?

Apple’s iPad lineup is incredibly strong, and two standout options are the iPad Air and iPad Pro. If you’re trying to decide whether the iPad Pro is worth the extra cost this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

Bonus pick: The all-new iPad mini is up to $100 off for Black Friday as well.

Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.

The iPad Air is available in 11-inch and 13-inch screen sizes, and uses an LCD display with a 60Hz refresh rate. This means it doesn’t offer OLED or ProMotion, unlike the iPad Pro. It uses Touch ID for biometric authentication, supports the Magic Keyboard and Apple Pencil Pro, and offers the full iPadOS multitasking experience.

The iPad Air is available in four colors: blue, purple, starlight, and space gray. It starts at 128GB of storage and can be configured up to 1TB.

The iPad Pro is the best iPad money can buy. It’s powered by Apple’s M5 chip and offers many advantages over the iPad Air.

The biggest difference is the display technology. The iPad Pro is available in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes and uses Apple’s Ultra Retina XDR display with tandem OLED technology. This means it offers deeper blacks, better contrast, and higher brightness than the LCD screen found in the iPad Air.

The iPad Pro also supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz. This means scrolling, animations, Apple Pencil interactions, and more will be significantly smoother.

Contrary to what the naming implies, the iPad Pro is also noticeably thinner and lighter than the iPad Air. The 11-inch iPad Pro measures 5.3mm thick, while the 13-inch model is even thinner at 5.1mm.

The iPad Pro offers Face ID instead of Touch ID, Thunderbolt connectivity, a four-speaker audio system, and nano-texture display options with the higher-end configuration.

For most people, the iPad Air is the right choice. It delivers the entire iPad experience, excellent performance, and comes in four fun colors and two different screen sizes.

The iPad Pro is the best iPad you can buy, but it’s overkill for most people. Don’t get me wrong, I love my iPad Pro. If it’s in your holiday budget, it’s a fantastic choice. I can’t overstate how impressive the tandem OLED display is. It’s significantly better than the LCD screen on the iPad Air. It’s also great having Face ID in the iPad form factor.

The iPad Pro is slightly more tempting at its current sale price, with the mid-range 13-inch model at an impressive $350 off.

Still, both the iPad Air and iPad Pro run the same iPadOS experience, and that’s why I think the iPad Air is the better value for most people. What do you think? Let us know down in the comments.

#3075. Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Microsoft announced two new AI models at Ignite 2026 that promise impressive performance for much lower cost. They could reshape its relationship with OpenAI and Anthropic for good.

At today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the company introduced two new frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks. But there’s a bigger story: what these models might mean for Microsoft’s AI costs and its dependence on OpenAI.

Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model shows 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Microsoft says MAI Code 2 offers comparable performance to GPT-6.1 Sol or Opus 5.5 at a fraction of the cost. Microsoft’s Code 2 Flash model is comparable to the lower-end GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5, also at considerably lower cost.

This doesn’t mean that those of us who pay for $100/month subscriptions will suddenly get the equivalent for five bucks. Instead, these are usage-based metrics based on API usage.

It’s also important to understand that the benchmarks are all Microsoft-provided. Performance numbers may well differ once the models undergo independent performance tests.

Throughout Satya Nadella’s keynote, Microsoft showed slides referencing a wide range of foundation models that are intended to work with Copilot and other Microsoft offerings. Microsoft famously has a multi-billion-dollar investment in OpenAI dating back to 2023, and has built many of its products and services around OpenAI intellectual property.

But now, Redmond is benchmarking its internally built models against Anthropic and OpenAI offerings, and also touting that it’s integrating these new models as optional choices for GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365, and Fabric.

Also: 75% of developers I surveyed prefer Claude Code over Codex

One thing that Nadella made clear in today’s keynote is how central AI is becoming in everything Microsoft does. Nearly all of those AI operations previously involved the company paying some token fees back to the frontier model providers or customers doing the same thing.

But with high-performing models of its own, Microsoft may become substantially less dependent on outside model providers, especially for the incredible volume of fairly basic and routine AI requests that occur across the company’s vast product line.

If you think back over the history of agentic work models like ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork, you may recall that they originated as agentic coding tools. As users adopted the coding harnesses in Claude Code and OpenAI Codex to off-label productivity applications, the AI companies noticed and packaged work-centric agentic tools that were more non-programmer-friendly.

Also: I let ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork loose on my files – only one made me nervous

There’s a lot of similarity between a coding agent and a work agent, including understanding a complex environment, using tools to change things, and producing reliable results. Coding turns out to be a very good environment for developing and testing these capabilities, particularly because code output is highly measurable. Coding agents are effective training grounds for non-coding work agents.

This becomes really interesting in today’s announcement. Along with Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, Microsoft announced MAI Work Flash, which it describes as having been derived from Code 2 Flash. Work Flash can help generate formulas in Excel, work with documents and instructions in Word, track decisions and extract useful information from Teams, and more.

Think about the level of intelligence these tasks are demanding from the AI models. Not that much. As long as the models are good enough, they’ll be good enough.

If Microsoft can reduce its expenses and use reliable models at a much lower price, the company itself will be able to save quite a bit of money across its entire software economy, while at the same time maintaining a deeper level of vertical integration and, therefore, control.

Let’s run some hypothetical numbers. Let’s say a company is spending $0.01 per AI request, which, with these new models, can drop down to $0.001 per request.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer very carefully first

A company with a daily inference cost of a million dollars (a company like Microsoft, for example) could drop that daily cost to about $100,000. Add that up across a year, and the change in models could save $325 million annually.

A million here, a million there. Pretty soon, you’re talking real money.

There’s no direct evidence that Microsoft is trying to produce replacement models for the frontier providers’ offerings. But it is an interesting and compelling story if we look at Microsoft developing its own engines for the software it sells.

Microsoft says the numbers it’s reporting at are using a 50% introductory discount. That’s why I measured against $0.001 per request instead of $0.0005 per request above.

Benchmark selection could be cherry-picking. The numbers are impressive. But as we all know, there are lies, damned lies, and benchmark results. I’m fairly sure Microsoft isn’t padding these numbers too much, because it benefits from the new models more than even its own customers, but still. It’s an open issue.

The company also described clearly that these new models are not designed to handle the most challenging agentic and research workloads. You’re probably not going to use them to solve a decades-old mathematics challenge. But you’re very likely to use them to reformat your PowerPoint.

Speaking of reformatting your PowerPoint, Microsoft also emphasized that these new models did unusually well on visualization assignments. That’s a very good fit for not only UI design challenges but also graphics and slide production.

#3073. Axon Enterprise vs. Palantir Technologies: Which Law Enforcement Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Axon's revenue jumped 33.6% while Palantir's surged 87.1%, but the valuation gap between the two is hard to ignore.

By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 24, 2026 at 3:00PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Axon Enterprise ›

Investors searching for exposure to mission-critical software and hardware often compare Axon Enterprise (AXON +3.81%) and Palantir Technologies (PLTR +1.14%). Both companies leverage sophisticated technology to solve complex problems for large institutions.

Axon specializes in public safety tools and cloud evidence management for law enforcement. Palantir provides massive data integration and artificial intelligence infrastructure for government and corporate clients. As both companies expand their digital platforms, determining which is the more attractive buy requires a look at their recent financial performance.

Axon Enterprise provides a comprehensive ecosystem of hardware and software designed for law enforcement and public safety professionals. Its product line includes Taser devices, body-worn cameras, and the Axon Evidence platform, which allows agencies to manage digital records securely. The company is actively expanding its presence among defense stocks and international markets across Europe and Asia. No single customer represented more than 10% of total net sales in 2025, which provides a diversified revenue base.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $3.4 billion, indicating a 33.6% increase compared to the prior period. This growth was accompanied by a net income of approximately $258.5 million. The company continues to transition customers toward subscription-based software services, which typically offer higher visibility into future sales. This steady growth suggests strong demand for its integrated safety solutions among federal and local agencies.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.6x. This ratio measures total debt relative to shareholder equity, showing how much the company relies on borrowed funds. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, is approximately 2.5x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was around $75.1 million. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 300% of operating cash flow, meaning reported cash generation is heavily inflated by this non-cash add-back.

Palantir Technologies develops platforms that integrate and analyze massive data sets to help organizations make better decisions. Its customer base is divided between government agencies and commercial enterprises, with a total of 954 customers as of late 2025. The company recently reported a remaining deal value of nearly $11.2 billion, split between its public and private sector contracts. Note that the top three customers accounted for roughly 16% of revenue in 2025. Customer concentration among these top clients adds a layer of risk to the business.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $7.3 billion, representing a significant 87% increase over the previous 12 months. Net income for this period was approximately $3.7 billion. This surge in performance is driven by the rapid adoption of its artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company often uses low-cost pilot deployments to prove the value of its software before moving to larger, long-term contracts.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.0x, showing the company has no debt relative to its equity. The current ratio is roughly 7.1x, indicating a strong ability to cover short-term financial obligations with existing assets. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow reached nearly $2.1 billion. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) accounted for roughly 32% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Axon Enterprise faces risks related to the acceptance of its products by law enforcement agencies. Negative publicity regarding its devices or software can impact demand. The company also faces global supply chain dependencies and rapid technological shifts, particularly in artificial intelligence. Legal risks include product liability claims and complex government procurement regulations. It competes in an environment alongside companies such as Motorola Solutions (MSI +0.04%).

Palantir Technologies carries risks associated with its revenue concentration, as a small number of customers provide a large portion of its total sales. The company also manages long and unpredictable sales cycles that require significant upfront investment. There is a risk that its AI technologies may fail to gain further market acceptance. Additionally, the company relies heavily on third-party cloud infrastructure from providers like Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN -1.21%) and Microsoft Corp. (MSFT +0.74%).

Palantir Technologies carries a notably higher valuation than Axon Enterprise when comparing both future earnings estimates and sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

Axon has a positive long-term outlook for growth as law enforcement is increasingly equipped with Tasers and the public is becoming increasingly demanding that agents wear body cameras. Its cloud-based evidence control system is also an increasingly sought-after service for law enforcement organization.

Expansion into Europe and Canada should also help, as should a focus on producing personal consumer-protection devices. In particular, all the data and video created by Axon customers have to be managed, and the company is seeing strong demand for its AI-based management systems from customers who find many of the services create efficiencies within their operations.

In fiscal 2026, sales are expected to grow well, up about a third to $3.6 billion, with net income of around $290 million and free cash flow of $425 million, well over 2025's levels. In 2027, consensus estimates project adding another $1 billion in revenue, with expanding net income and free cash flow as well.

Palantir started out as a tech contractor to the U.S. military and law enforcement, and the federal government still accounts for half of its revenue. But the business has been successfully expanding beyond government work, with about a quarter of sales coming from international customers and a significant minority of revenue from the private sector. For the first time last quarter, private sector revenue exceeded U.S. government revenue.

Palantir says customers are drawn to its sovereign AI, which is its term for systems that can help build themselves while protecting what makes each system the AI is refining, so it is not commoditized. Companies like Nvidia Corp. (NVDA -5.86%) and L3Harris Technologies (LHX +1.27%) are notable customers of Palantir's sovereign AI.

The boom in private-sector AI business should double Palantir's 2026 sales to $8.6 billion, with a $2.7 billion jump in net income to $4.4 billion. 2027 should see continued fast growth, with consensus analysts' estimates projecting revenue of $13.1 billion and net income over $6 billion.

The top-line growth of Palantir is difficult to ignore, but its shares trade at an exceptional premium that may not account for the long-term threat of AI displacing its business. Axon comes at a premium, too, as seen through its P/E and P/S ratios, but it's cheaper than Palantir, and the company is delivering exceptional sales growth and improving margins. For 2027, go with Axon Enterprise.

#3072. Even the Iconic Google Home Page Can’t Survive the Push for More AI

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

The search giant is revamping Google.com with AI options.

This is not your parents’ Google home page. In its push to get more users to adopt its AI tools, the search engine giant is rolling out a raft of new features worldwide.

The new elements include three new buttons below the search bar at Google.com: Create images, Ask about files and Brainstorm. The Google Search button is gone, but the I’m Feeling Lucky button remains.

The buttons are available when using Google on a desktop but not on mobile. I was able to see the new buttons when signed in to my Google account.

When signed out, I was only able to see the typical home page, with the only AI button being AI Mode, which has been there since May 2025.

Clicking on the “Create images” button opens up a new page where you can create an AI-generated image using Google’s Nano Banana. It’s the same image-generation tool you can use on other Google platforms such as the Gemini app, Google AI Studio and AI Mode in Search.

Clicking “Ask about files” allows for several options. You can have the AI analyze a document and rewrite it, simply have it answer questions or ask it to perform tasks such as “polish my resume” or “draft an email with action items.”

The “Brainstorm” button prompts you to “describe your goal,” such as making a to-do list, learning how to code or finding a table at a restaurant.

Another new feature, as announced by Google Search Product VP Robby Stein on X, is a collapsible sidebar on the left side of the home page, which shows your recent AI search threads and offers the ability to create a new one:

Stein said the new sidebar will help users go back to where they left off.

“People are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done — and in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web,” Stein posted.

I didn’t see the collapsible sidebar during my testing of the home page.

Google has integrated its Gemini AI models throughout its various platforms — Search, Gmail, Docs, Pixel phones and third-party apps such as Adobe, Shopify, OpenTable and Instacart. This past week, Google announced several other new AI features — integrations with stores such as Albertsons, Safeway and Target to complete orders and connect to apps such as Peloton and Adobe.

Over the summer, Google’s Gemini app topped 1 billion users in what CEO Sundar Pichai called the company’s “fastest growing product ever.”

But Google’s rush to force-feed AI into its products has met with plenty of pushback. The New York City, Los Angeles and Chicago school districts said they might choose different search engines because Google said it will not remove AI from search tools used by students, The New York Times reported.

Google said search and the Gemini app will be turned off for schools unless school administrators want them. But Google said there will not be a chatbot-free version of search available for schools. So schools declining AI will not be able to search using Google at all.

Google’s AI Overviews, which appear at the top of many search page results, have also been blamed for a steep drop in web traffic to content publishers. AI Overviews summarize user search queries and replace the long list of blue hyperlinks that once appeared across search pages. So instead of clicking on those links to get more information, giving publishers valuable clicks, a user can simply get their query response by reading the AI Overview.

#3071. Things 3.25 update brings new touch features to the MacBook Pro

Cultured Code is bringing swipe gestures to Things on Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro. Version 3.25 builds on the task manager’s basic touch support so you can schedule a to-do with a swipe or select several tasks with two fingers and drag them all at once.

Say you’re going through your Today list and want to put something off until tomorrow. Swipe right on the to-do to open the date picker. Open it by touch and you’ll see taller rows that make dates easier to tap. Custom menus get the same treatment.

Swiping left selects a to-do. Swipe left again to deselect it. For a longer list, swipe up or down with two fingers to select several items at once. Then touch and hold any selected item to pick up the whole group, even if some of those tasks are offscreen. You can also drag individual to-dos and headings.

A single tap selects a to-do, and a second tap expands it. Double-tapping works too. Inside a to-do, checklist items are easier to reorder by touch. You can also cancel a to-do or checklist item by pressing and holding its checkbox.

Cultured Code has also made the sidebar easier to resize with a finger and given buttons throughout the Mac app larger tap targets.

The update follows Siri AI and Spotlight integration in Things 3.24 and more flexible scheduling for repeating to-dos in Things 3.23. You can find Things for Mac on the Mac App Store.

#3070. Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft could reshape enterprise spending, but there's a critical difference between estimated value and money saved.

We all know AI can get expensive. But does that expense result in real business value? That’s the trillion-dollar question Microsoft aims to answer with today’s introduction of Agent 365 Business Analytics.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

Earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees. With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft is attempting to build an accounting system for AI labor. The system attempts to calculate the economic value of the work performed by agents compared with what the agents cost, and then provide a return on investment estimate.

If it works, this is some very cool stuff. Microsoft is trying to map labor-market economics onto AI usage data to create value estimates.

Also: Work IQ is Microsoft’s big bet on agent-first enterprise IT, and I have questions

To do so, it uses real labor-costing information, including data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the O*NET database from the US Department of Labor, and its own LinkedIn Occupational Graph.

This data, along with data gathered from Agent 365, is aggregated into analysis intended to answer:

The goal is to provide a comprehensive picture of AI spend against value produced.

Software accounting is long established and straightforward. We measure subscription fees, cost per seat, compute costs, burden costs (like floor space and other infrastructure), and more. But AI work doesn’t fit that model, making it very hard to quantify value.

Instead, Agent 365 Business Analytics measures cost both relative to human labor and in terms of technological expense. For example, it might look at a task and determine how much human effort that task would normally take, and then price that effort based on prevailing common labor rates.

Then, it might factor in how much of the task was actually done by a human vs. how much was contributed by an AI, along with the estimated value of the AI’s contribution. Then it mixes in the actual AI processing cost (whether in subscriptions, tokens, on-premises infrastructure, and cloud support).

Also: These Claude Enterprise features let you track AI ROI – what’s new

What comes out is a hybrid labor estimate that combines human contribution, human-replacement savings, AI costs, and then potentially AI savings over human costs. It sounds positively Orwellian. But the bottom line is that companies really haven’t been able to understand the AI bottom line.

There’s a catch. All these numbers are estimates. In its blog post, Redmond specifically says, “Assisted hours are a directional estimate of work AI helped complete, not measured time saved or financial return.”

In other words, what Agent 365 Business Analytics estimates might not actually line up with real-world experience or expenses. It’s also possible that AI work might have been assigned because there was AI to do the work, not that the AI was saving company labor costs with every token processed.

In other words, Microsoft may be able to tell you the economic value of AI-assisted work, but it can’t demonstrate definitively that the company saved any real money.

Also: 5 reasons your company needs a chief AI officer in 2026

I find it particularly telling that this is from the company that makes PowerPoint. Because now, with Agent 365 Business Analytics, it’s entirely possible that you could produce economic dashboards that look really, really impressive, but are entirely irrelevant to real life.

That’s not to say the product is useless. But it does go to the idea that you will have to be quite disciplined in how you interpret the results and how much stock you put in them for decision-making. It is one source of possible truth, not the source of absolute truth.

Microsoft has been investing for decades to build out the core infrastructure of enterprise computing. AI isn’t any different when it comes to the company’s overall mission.

With Agent 365 and the company’s related offerings, Microsoft wants to help you:

This means the company doesn’t necessarily have to provide you with the AI model to help you run your enterprise. With integration with offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic, Salesforce, Google, Databricks, Snowflake, and others, the company doesn’t even have to provide the apps or SaaS capabilities.

But if it can get in there and manage your plumbing, help you control costs, and be the HR operation for your AI workforce, Microsoft could own a central piece of your business’s operations.

#3069. New Hyundai Elantra Hybrid Debuts With 53 Mpg, AI in the Dash

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

The redesigned compact sedan features Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant, Gleo AI, and an updated regenerative braking system with EV-like one-pedal driving.

Hyundai pulled back the cover on the new 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class. The bold styling may not be for everyone — though, personally, I dig it — but economy car shoppers will certainly be interested in the compact hybrid sedan’s targeted 53 mpg and Gleo, Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant that controls the automaker’s new Android Automotive OS-based dashboard tech.

The humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an important one for the brand. It’s the automaker’s second-bestselling vehicle, behind only the Tucson. More importantly, the Elantra is one of the stalwarts of the affordable compact sedan class, a segment that many US automakers have abandoned in favor of more profitable SUVs. At a time when buyers are more sensitive than ever to inflated fuel costs and sticker prices, economy car options like the Elantra and its second-generation hybrid powertrain are worth our attention.

The updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox. Combined output at the front wheels rises to 155 horsepower (up from 139 hp in the current car), thanks to a more powerful 45-kilowatt electric-assist motor (up from 32kW).

An updated regenerative braking system recaptures energy when slowing and now offers an “EV-like one-pedal driving experience” that can bring the car to a complete stop at its maximum setting. Additionally, the hybrid now features a new Stay mode that lets the climate control and infotainment systems run while parked for up to 30 minutes without firing up the gas engine.

Sharing the stage in LA, the new nonhybrid Elantra arrives with the same 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine and continuously variable transmission as the current generation. At 147 hp with a target of 35 mpg combined, it’s no more powerful than before, but it should also be no less efficient, despite the sedan’s increased size. I’d say the hybrid is the better choice, though it will likely also be the more expensive powertrain option.

Inside, a new cockpit design moves the now-hoodless digital instrument cluster, a 9.9-inch “Slim Information Display,” away from the driver and toward the windshield on the dashboard. The new placement, similar to what I’ve seen on recent Toyota models, puts vehicle information closer to the driver’s line of sight.

Pleos Connect, Hyundai’s new Android Automotive OS-based infotainment suite, lives on a 12.9-inch center display. Despite being based on Android, it still features the automaker’s bespoke navigation and media software, rather than Google Maps. The system is said to be over-the-air updatable and features standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto for drivers who’d rather bring their own apps on the road.

The Pleos dashboard OS is matched with Gleo AI (who names these things?!), which is Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant that lets drivers and passengers talk to the car rather than occupy a hand on the touchscreen. Hyundai says the system features “contextual language support, multi-command capability and zone-specific recognition,” which basically means the car knows who’s talking to it and which seat they’re in and can assign context to voice prompts based on the situation.

“Affordable doesn’t have to be anonymous,” said Olabisi Boyle, Hyundai’s senior vice president of product, at the unveiling. I agree: Hyundai’s designers clearly aren’t afraid to push the design envelope, and the new Elantra is anything but bland.

The sedan introduces the automaker’s Art of Steel design language, with chunky flared fenders that feel inspired by the brand’s recent new SUVs. The tall greenhouse looks a bit cartoonish if you catch it at the wrong angle, but it provides increased headroom inside. From certain angles, the sedan’s beefy fenders remind me of an angular Korean take on the Subaru WRX. From other viewpoints, I can see inspiration from Hyundai’s N Vision 74 concept and the hydrogen-fueled Nexo, particularly in the triangular rear windows.

The sedan measures 188.8 inches bumper-to-bumper on a 108.3-inch wheelbase that is 1.2 inches longer than the current model’s. Hyundai says the stretch for this generation improves rear-passenger space, now rated at 39.1 inches of legroom on the second row. The Elantra, according to its designers, now approaches the interior volume of a midsize car, a claim I’d take with a grain of salt had I not watched multiple six-foot-plus attendees slip into the back seat with relative ease.

Hyundai did not announce pricing or detailed specs at the auto show debut, and availability is still vague. However, based on the stated model years, which are usually slightly offset from calendar years, I expect the 2027 Elantra sedan to arrive in early 2027, with the 2028 Elantra Hybrid following in late 2027.

Editors’ note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Genesis. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

#3068. Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026, plus more AI workplace updates

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

The company also released new ROI tracking tools for companies monitoring their AI spend.

AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

During the keynote for the company’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella announced Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several new Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

“As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft said. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”

Microsoft also announced Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft said, and assign it tasks.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s new Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector

Microsoft said the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

“Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft said.

The company added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

Nadella also announced a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. Currently in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

“The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up quickly,” Microsoft said of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill

Microsoft also announced that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can quickly rack up costs when unsupervised.

Microsoft announced a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Agent 365, which Microsoft announced last year, is the company’s observability platform. Microsoft said Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft showed how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

“It starts with a new way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft said. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”

Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

“Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft said. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise plans.

#3065. Micron vs. Sandisk: Which AI Memory Stock Is the Better Buy?

Both of these AI memory stocks still have triple-digit returns in 2026 despite selloffs since this summer.

By Dave Kovaleski – Nov 24, 2026 at 3:05PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Micron Technology ›

It has been a wild ride in 2026 for two leading memory chip stocks, Micron (MU -11.01%) and Sandisk (SNDK -11.13%).

Both are among Wall Street’s best performers year to date, but their paths to those returns have been extremely volatile.

At its 2026 closing high of $1,213 per share on June 25, Micron was up about 326% year to date. At its split-adjusted closing peak of $291 per share on June 22, Sandisk was up 870%.

Since then, Sandisk has lost 68% of its value, falling to $91 per share. But it's still up 209% from $30 per share at the start of the year. Micron had fallen 51% to $594 per share on Nov. 20, but bounced back on Nov. 23, climbing to $717 per share. It's still up 147% from $285 per share at the start of the year.

So, if you’ve owned shares since before this summer, you're still probably happy with the returns, despite the wild swings. But heading into 2027, which of the two is the better buy?

Both Sandisk and Micron have benefited from the current memory and storage supercycle, which was brought on by the fast advance of artificial intelligence computing. Demand for AI memory and storage has been magnified by the massive amount of AI infrastructure being built by hyperscalers, neoclouds, and others, and, in turn, chipmakers such as Nvidia, Intel, and Advanced Micro Devices.

The demand for chips that can provide quickly accessible memory and storage for the data AI requires and creates has boomed as a result. Because memory chips are essentially a commodity, the companies that manufacture them try to avoid overbuilding their production capacity. In the wake of the rapid surge in demand, they now can't keep up. This has given Micron, Sandisk, and their peers incredible pricing power and huge backlogs of orders.

While Micron and Sandisk have products that do directly compete with each other, their respective cash cow products are in separate areas. Micron's main product is high bandwidth memory (HBM) chips for AI data centers that can provide fast memory for AI processing. It is mostly sold out of HBM through 2027. Sandisk's main products are NAND and solid-state storage drives, which provide long-term data storage for AI computing.

Both memory giants also have long-term contracts with major hyperscalers and customers with commitments through at least 2030.

Sandisk just underwent an 8-for-1 stock split on Nov. 20, which brought its previously lofty share price down to a more accessible $91 per share.

Though both of these stocks have dropped so sharply over the past few months, that was mostly due to factors beyond their business performance. Many investors took profits when the stocks were higher. They were also brought down by broader concerns about whether the enormous levels of spending on AI infrastructure will deliver the return on investment that the bulls promise. The downtrend was likely exacerbated by the U.S. midterm elections, in which voters in many locales made it clear that they want stricter regulatory and government controls around data center development. This has led to concerns that hyperscalers might negotiate down or out of their long-term chip deals.

The Jensen Huang Nvidia situation did not help AI stocks either, although he was just reinstated as CEO on Monday, so we'll see where that leads.

The fact remains that both Sandisk and Micron are vital suppliers in the AI boom, and even if there are more controls on where data centers can go and a greater level of concern for their environmental impact, that won't eliminate the need for AI processing and storage.

Also, both of these stocks are dirt cheap, made even cheaper by the recent sell-off. This is a testament to their massive earnings power. Micron is trading at just 3.4 times 1-year forward earnings. Sandisk is even cheaper with a 1-year forward P/E of 2.5. And both have minuscule 1-year forward price/earnings-to-growth ratios of about 0.05.

I own shares of Micron and will add more at this low valuation, but Sandisk is also a screaming buy.

#3064. Genesis Launches Hybrids at the LA Auto Show, EREV Coming in 2027

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Genesis adds a 347-horsepower hybrid powertrain to its most popular G80 sedan and GV80 SUV, and teases a 640-mile extended-range EV for early 2027.

Korean luxury automaker Genesis launched its first hybrid models this week, debuting new powertrains for the G80 sedan and GV80 SUV at the 2026 LA Auto Show. The company says the electrified system is both more efficient and more powerful than the current nonhybrid versions. For buyers who want a more battery-focused experience, Genesis teased an upcoming 640-mile extended-range electric vehicle due to arrive in early 2027.

The hybridized versions of the brand’s most popular sedan and SUV arrive as American drivers show growing interest in energy-efficient cars, both battery electrics and hybrids, driven by high fuel costs and better understanding of the technologies. Hybrids, in particular, have attracted attention because they behave like traditional combustion cars: There’s no need to install home charging hardware or change familiar driving and refueling habits. Just get in and reap better fuel economy with every mile.

The G80 Hybrid and GV80 Hybrid share a 2.5-liter turbocharged hybrid powertrain. Genesis says the system is 16% more powerful than the gasoline-only version, outputting 347 horsepower and 391 pound-feet of torque. A new liquid-cooled battery pack improves thermal management and allows higher maximum discharge than Hyundai Motor Group’s previous air-cooled hybrid batteries, boosting performance. Both models use a seven-speed automatic transmission adapted to work with the electric motor’s regenerative braking.

Genesis hasn’t announced official fuel economy estimates, but says the G80 Hybrid is 30% more efficient than the standard model, while the GV80 Hybrid is 24% more efficient. Based on current EPA figures, my math puts them in the ballpark of 30 mpg and 27 mpg, respectively. Any improvement is good, but those aren’t exactly earth-shattering gains. We’ll have to wait for the official ratings to be sure.

Each hybrid can be toggled into a silent EV mode for short distances — good for gliding into a driveway, garage or parking deck without waking the neighbors. However, without a plug, all the energy in the battery ultimately comes from the gas tank.

A new Stay Mode lets owners run the climate control and infotainment without starting the engine for around 30 minutes. I like to think of it as the “moment of zen in the driveway before you have to go inside and face responsibility” mode, or maybe the “eating lunch in your car” mode. It’s similar to Toyota’s My Room Mode on its hybrids.

Aside from the powertrain, the G80 and GV80 Hybrids are largely identical to their combustion counterparts. Hybrid-specific touches include a three-dimensional G-Matrix grille inlay redesigned for these models, as well as new exterior colors.

Inside, a 27-inch OLED display combining the instrument cluster and navigation stretches halfway across the dashboard. Tech features include Digital Key 2 Premium, which lets owners use their phone instead of a key fob to unlock and start the car, and active road noise cancellation. Genesis’ driver-assistance suite is headlined by the Highway Drive Assist 2 steering assistance system and the Remote Smart Parking Assist 2, which enables automatic parking with the driver inside or just nearby the car.

Prices for the sedan and SUV haven’t been announced. Final specifications and EPA fuel economy figures are expected closer to the early 2027 launch window.

My cynical side says that these new models are just Genesis doing what Toyota has done since the RX 400h debuted in 2004. (To be fair, Genesis didn’t become an independent brand until 2015, so its rival has a bit of a head start.) In practical terms, the move brings Hyundai Motor Group’s luxury brand into parity with other group members and luxury car competitors that have rolled out updated hybrids over the last year, and meets customers’ increasing demand for more energy-efficient cars where they are.

In addition to its first hybrid sedan and SUV, Genesis executives announced that the brand will expand the availability of its wild-styled, high-performance GV60 Magma full-electric SUV to more states and markets to meet higher-than-expected demand.

At the debut event in LA, the brand also teased an upcoming extended-range EV — an EV with an onboard gasoline generator, essentially a very advanced plug-in hybrid — set to launch in early 2027. The EREV model is targeting over 640 miles before its “all-new high-performance battery” and gas tank both run dry, but Genesis didn’t give further details about the upcoming model.

Editor’s note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Genesis. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

#3063. Microsoft’s new Licensed Weights lets businesses customize AI models with their own data

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Microsoft is bridging the gap between proprietary and open-weight AI while targeting data-conscious businesses.

During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5

MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

“You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, said during the keynote.

The approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft said it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman said during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

The dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the company has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

Western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman said of the new coding model the company announced at Ignite.

The company also released its new image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

#3062. CarPlay Ultra coming to these cars, according to Apple

Last year, Apple officially announced CarPlay Ultra, the next-generation version of CarPlay that it first teased way back at WWDC 2022.

CarPlay Ultra first launched for Aston Martin owners in the United States and Canada. What about other automakers? Here’s what we know.

9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off. These deliver immersive 360 Spatial Sound, active noise canceling, low-latency wireless connectivity, and much more.

Updated November 24, 2026: Latest on Hyundai, more.

In December 2023, Apple said that Porsche and Aston Martin would be the first automakers to support next-generation CarPlay starting in 2024. That deadline came and went, and Apple confirmed in January that next-gen CarPlay had been delayed but was still in development.

Apple doesn’t offer a timeline on when CarPlay Ultra will actually be available through any other brand beyond Aston Martin. The company also does not have a dedicated list of automakers that have signed on to support CarPlay Ultra listed on its website.

When Apple announced the next-generation version of CarPlay at WWDC 2022, however, it stated that several brands had committed to supporting the platform. In May of last year, Apple touted that three new partners had signed on: Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis.

However, several brands have also dropped their plans to support CarPlay Ultra. Mercedes-Benz was originally on Apple’s list, but abandoned its plans to support next-generation CarPlay in 2024. According to the Financial Times, Audi, Volvo, Polestar, and Renault have also decided against supporting CarPlay Ultra, despite originally being touted as partners by Apple.

With all of that said, here is the full list of automakers who plan to eventually support CarPlay Ultra, as of April 2026.

What do we know beyond this list? Not a whole lot. Interestingly, Top Gear reported that the Hyundai IONIQ 3 EV would support CarPlay Ultra. Hyundai announced the IONIQ 3 in April, but has not commented on whether the vehicle will support CarPlay Ultra as rumors suggested.

Mark Gurman at Bloomberg has also reported CarPlay Ultra will launch for “least one major new Hyundai/Kia model in the second half of this year.”

While Apple has touted Ford as a partner for CarPlay Ultra, the automaker recently signaled it’s not too impressed with the first version of a platform.

In a recent interview, Ford CEO Jim Farley was asked whether the company is “considering” CarPlay Ultra support. Here’s what he said:

“We are. We don’t like the execution in round 1 of Ultra, but we’re very committed to Apple. I’ve talked to Tim many times about this.”

It’s better than a flat “no,” but perhaps not the enthusiasm Ford drivers might have hoped to hear.

The question at this point is whether any other automakers have ditched CarPlay Ultra. Ideally, Apple will provide a full list sooner rather than later, but in the meantime, this is the only information we have.

Learn more about everything new with CarPlay Ultra in our dedicated coverage.

#3061. Cmb.Tech (CMBT) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Strong tanker rates and asset sales shaped the quarter, with ammonia ambitions in focus.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Cmb.Tech (CMBT +4.22%) reported a quarter of elevated profitability driven by record tanker spot rates and strategic asset sales. Management focused on the transition toward ammonia-powered shipping while maintaining a diversified fleet across dry bulk, container, and offshore energy segments. The company stated its intention to prioritize balance sheet deleveraging and consistent dividend distributions as its heavy capital expenditure cycle approaches completion. Strategic initiatives highlighted during the call included the operational debut of the world's first ammonia-powered iron ore carrier and the expansion of bauxite trade demand.

Alexander Saverys: Good afternoon, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Cmb.Tech's earnings conference call for the third quarter of 2026. My name is Alexander Saverys.
